#+TITLE: DIRECT Variant Surface — selection × partitioning × refinement control × hidden constraints
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: direct-variants

* Summary

The papers license a large, well-measured variant surface: three selection schemes (IO/IA/GL) × four partitioning schemes (N-DTC/1-DTC/1-DTDV/1-DBDP), plus refinement-control add-ons (epsilon, delta-limit, median/average, globally-biased, rev) and a hidden-constraint surrogate (DIRECT-GLh). For a 6-DOF search at 20k–35k evaluations, the literature says the current repo configuration — original-DIRECT selection with ε=0 and all ties, 1-DTC partition, L2 size — sits in the worst local-refinement regime; the highest-evidence upgrade is the GL (two-step Pareto) selection combined with 1-DTC or 1-DBDP partitioning, optionally with the globally-biased (-gb) phase switch for refinement control, and the GLh φ = f_min + d(x_min,x) surrogate if unrenderable poses produce NaN. The "restrictions hurt cheap functions" finding (Mathematics 2022, 10, 3760) is real and worse when f_min ≈ 0 (the silhouette-cost shape), and -gb is indeed the only restriction that never hurt in that study — it was also the best on expensive functions. Every variant below can be expressed as an Options struct on DirectOptimizer with bit-identical defaults, and scored headlessly on a DIRECTGOLib/GKLS battery under the production cumulative-budget shape.

* Key Findings

** Finding 1: The repo's current configuration is the literature's worst-case local-refinement regime
- The extracted optimizer is original-DIRECT selection (Jarvis convex hull) with ε=0, selecting *all* hull points including equal-slope ties (`slope >= highest_slope`), trisecting one (largest denormalized) side, L2 size measure (norm of the side vector), center sampling. [Source: /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp L93-141, L143-200; /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/data_structures_6D.cpp L107-128]
- Jones & Martins 2021: "with ε=0 DIRECT spends so many evaluations refining local minima that it ends up far from the optimum after 3000 evaluations" (Shubert); the ε=0 regime allows "excessive local search". The ε|f_min| rule is what protects the original DIRECT from this — the repo has no such rule at all. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 (JOG 79:521–566, DOI 10.1007/s10898-020-00952-6), §3.3/Fig. 19]
- The empirical study's "IO" (improved original) scheme restricts ties to one candidate per (size,value) group; the repo selects all ties, which the study and Jones & Martins show increases "global drag" and slows convergence ("Best results are achieved by ignoring ties for potentially optimal rectangles, only trisecting on one side, and using Gablonsky's modified definition of rectangle size" — Figure 18). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §2.1.1; https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 §3.2]
- Confidence: high (code-verified against primary literature).
- Relevance: the 20k trunk budget is exactly the regime where ε=0 over-refinement wastes evaluations; tie-all selection adds drag on top. Both are cheap to fix (hull tie-break + optional ε filter) with bit-identical defaults preserved.

** Finding 2: GL selection beats IO/IA by ~60–72% on n>4 problems — the regime the 6-DOF search lives in
- On 96 DIRECTGOLib v1.1 box-constrained problems: GL-based variants failed 19/384 cases vs IO 63/384 and IA 55/384; GL required ~60% (vs IO) and ~62% (vs IA) fewer function evaluations overall, and ~72% fewer on n>4 problems. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4.2]
- Budget-regime crossover (operational characteristics, n>4 multimodal): at ≤500 evals IO variants lead; at ~1000–4000 N-DTC-IO is best (~50% solved); at ≥4000 evals the GL variants (1-DTC-GL, 1-DBDP-GL) are the most efficient. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 Fig. 7, §4.2]
- Partitioning for n>4: 1-DBDP-based variants best average (≈16% fewer evals than N-DTC-based); 1-DTDV "very inefficient for higher dimensional test problems"; 1-DTDV shines only when most solution coordinates sit on the boundary (ν≥8/10 coordinates: 551 evals vs 6,487 for N-DTC-IO on Levy10; but 141,999 vs 919 when interior). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4.1, Table 3]
- On 800 GKLS problems (n=2–5, simple+hard classes): 1-DTC-IO best average (8,021) and best median (1,427); 1-DBDP-GL ranks 5th there but is best on simple classes at budgets >400 evals; IO wins on hard GKLS classes. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §5, Table 6]
- Confidence: high (directly from the study's tables; the study is the repo's own evidence base, papers/ 2022 PDF).
- Relevance: 6-DOF = n>4; 20k trunk = well above the 4000-eval crossover → GL selection is the evidence-backed choice; the partition choice is a tradeoff (1-DTC: best GKLS median + minimal change from current code; 1-DBDP: best n>4 average but requires diagonal-bisection rework). 1-DTDV is a trap unless the pose optimum is confirmed near the range boundary.

** Finding 3: The DIRECT-GLh hidden-constraint surrogate is applicable to NaN/unrenderable poses at negligible cost
- GLh assigns infeasible midpoints the surrogate φ = f_min + d(x_min, x) (Euclidean distance in the *normalized unit cube*), normalized via f̄(x)=(f−f_min)/(f_max−f_min) and d̄=d/d_max so objective and distance are commensurate; f̄_min ≡ 0 drops out. Infeasible points never become f_min (min over feasible only). [Source: thesis §5.2, DOI 10.15388/vu.thesis.138 (mif.vu.lt PDF); DIRECTGO code /tmp clone Algorithms/sDirect_GLh.m Selection()]
- Cost is minimal: the distances d(x_min, x) are *already computed* for the GL two-step selection (the local step is Pareto on (size, distance)); per-iteration cost is one O(N) pass to re-tag infeasible values whenever f_min improves. "Such a technique does not require any additional computation." [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 (DIRECTGO, ACM TOMS 48(4), DOI 10.1145/3559755) §2.3; sDirect_GLh.m]
- Performance on hidden-constraint problems (constraint info withheld, 80 problems): DIRECT-GLh failed 18/80 vs DIRECT-NAS 29/80, DIRECT-Barrier 46/80, subDIRECT-Barrier 47–53/80; GLh took ~4.5× fewer iterations and ~33× less time than NAS. [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 §4.2.1, Table 5]
- DirectGO's own description of why alternatives fail: NaN-valued boxes "would not be selected as potential optimal at all"; barrier penalties leave feasible-edge exploration very slow. [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 §2.3]
- The repo currently passes NaN/Inf straight into storage: `EvaluateCostFunction` has no finite-check; a NaN result fails `result < current_optimum_value_` so it never becomes the optimum, but NaN boxes enter the storage matrix and poison hull slopes in `ConvexHull` (NaN slope comparisons). [Source: /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp L203-220, L93-141]
- Confidence: high for the algorithm and cost; medium for *whether the production GPU silhouette cost actually emits NaN* — no NaN handling exists anywhere in the C++ cost path (only Qt UI validation in app/experimental/PoseBridge.cpp L177-184), so the trigger condition is unverified.
- Relevance: if the GPU cost can fail (degenerate poses, empty silhouette), GLh converts silent corruption into a directed search toward feasibility — and the needed distance data is already there once GL selection lands.

** Finding 4: Refinement control — "restrictions hurt cheap functions" is confirmed, and -gb is the only safe one
- Mathematics 2022, 10, 3760 tested six refinement-reduction add-ons on 1-DTC-GL over 287 DIRECTGOLib v1.2 problems: success rates 1-DTC-GL-gb 0.7840 (225/287) > 1-DTC-GL 0.7805 (224/287) > -limit 0.7631 > -min 0.7526 > -rev 0.7317 > -median 0.7073 > -average 0.6551. Every restriction except gb hurt the base algorithm; gb is "the only algorithm with the same or better performance than the original 1-DTC-GL". [Source: https://epublications.vu.lt/object/elaba:143490244/143490244.pdf Table 2, §3, §4]
- "In the case of cheap test functions, the original 1-DTC-GL is the best of all the algorithms tested, meaning that the local refinement reduction schemes are redundant. However, when the objective functions are expensive, the local refinement reduction techniques improve the performance, and 1-DTC-GL-gb is the best technique among all tested." [Source: same, §3–§4]
- The restriction harm is worst when f_min = 0: "the restriction on selecting small hyper-rectangles may prevent the algorithms from converging to a solution... especially apparent when the solution is equal to zero" (1-DTC-GL-average worsened average evals by 32% overall; suffered most on f*=0 problems). [Source: same, §3]
- gb mechanics (from the DIRECTGO implementation of the studied algorithm): run the traditional two-step selection; after 5 consecutive iterations without f_min improvement, drop the local (distance-based) selection phase, except every 5th iteration ("security" iteration) — `(fMinNotImpr > 5) && (mod(fMinNotImpr,5) ~= 0)` → local phase else global-only. Defaults `ovexpl='GL'`, `locbalance='GL'`, `ep=1e-4`. [Source: /tmp clone of https://github.com/blockchain-group/DIRECTGO, Algorithms/I_DTC_GL.m L122-138, L235-237; GENDIRECT parameter table in README]
- Jones & Martins: the ε=1e-4 default protects the original DIRECT from ε=0's excessive local search; adaptive-ε (Finkel-Kelley DIRECT-restart) is mixed (better on Shubert, worse on Powell-48). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 §2.3.2, §3.3]
- Confidence: high (direct quotes from the study that owns this exact question).
- Relevance: JTML's silhouette cost has f_min ≈ 0 and a GPU eval that is expensive (dilation 6/3/1 renders) — the two conditions where restrictions fail and where gb pays. ε-based restrictions (min/median/average) are doubly contraindicated (window ε|f_min| collapses at f_min→0 — the Sergeyev–Kvasov zero-minimum weakness Jones & Martins reproduce). Answer to Q3: yes, -gb is the only refinement control that survives; for cheap analytic battery functions keep it OFF and test the crossover.

** Finding 5: The full variant surface maps onto an Options struct with bit-identical defaults
- The DIRECTGO toolbox exposes exactly this surface as options: `locbalance` ∈ {GL, gb, rev} and `ovexpl` ∈ {GL, min, median, average, limit} on the I_DTC_GL family; GENDIRECT generalizes to Partitioning{Strategy: DTC/DTDV/DTCS/DBVS/DBDP/DBVD/DBC, SubSides: All/One}, Selection{AggrFuncVal, CandMeasure: Diagonal/LongSide, Strategy: Original/Aggressive/Pareto/RedPareto, EqualCand: All/One, SolRefin: Min/Median/Average/Off, Ep: 1e-4, ControlEp: Off/Restart/MultiLevel1/MultiLevel2, GloballyBiased: Off/On, TwoPhase: Off/On}. [Source: https://github.com/blockchain-group/DIRECTGO README, GENDIRECT table; Algorithms/I_DTC_GL.m header]
- The 12 studied variants are the cross-product IO/IA/GL × N-DTC/1-DTC/1-DTDV/1-DBDP; N-DTC-GL ≡ DIRECT-GL; 1-DBDP-GL ≡ GL-selected BIRECT; the study's IO and BIRECT/DIRECT differ only in the tie restriction. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §3, Table 1]
- Repo mapping: selection mode → `ConvexHull()` (L93-141; add ε post-filter, tie restriction, Pareto front, aggressive), split rule + sampling → `TrisectPotentiallyOptimal()` (L143-200; currently 1-DTC-alike: one side, largest denormalized, center sampling — a coincidence worth pinning), size measure → `HyperBox6D::size_` (L107-128; L2 norm of sides; Gablonsky L∞ = half longest side is the alternative), hidden constraints → `EvaluateCostFunction()` (L203-220) + a feasibility flag in `DirectDataStorage`, budgets → already parametric (`budget_` + `SetCallOffset`, Run() L30-67; settings_constants.h TRUNK_BUDGET=20000, BRANCH_BUDGET=5000×2, Z_SEARCH_BUDGET=5000).
- Defaults must reproduce today's bit-identical search: selection=original-ε=0-all-ties, split=1-DTC-largest-denormalized-side, size=L2, hidden=off — every new Options field defaults to current behavior (R13 pin).
- Confidence: high (code + DIRECTGO source verified).
- Relevance: the harness (angle 03) can then score variants by swapping one Options value; defaults unchanged means the Tier-1/Tier-2 golden gates still hold for the baseline config.

** Finding 6: The analytic battery exists in the papers and is headless-portable
- DIRECTGOLib v1.1: 96 box-constrained problems, n ∈ {2,5,10}, known f*, domains; includes Hartman6 (n=6, f*=−3.3223), Goldstein-Price (n=2, f*=3.0), Shekel 5/7/10 (n=4), and n=5 variants of Ackley/Alpine/Griewank/Rastrigin/Rosenbrock/Schwefel/Levy/Michalewicz/Styblinski-Tang — the last being the closest analytic stand-in for 6-DOF pose search. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 Appendix A Table 7; library at https://github.com/blockchain-group/DIRECTGOLib, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.6491951]

[Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4; arXiv:2107.02205 §4]

[Source: /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/test/unit/test_direct_optimizer.cpp]

* Variant Surface (12 + refinement add-ons)

** Selection schemes
- IO — Improved Original: lower-right convex hull of (size, f(center)) with ε in eq. (4), ties restricted to one candidate per (size,value) group. Current repo = this *without* ε and *with* all ties.
- IA — Improved Aggressive: select the min-value box of every distinct size group, with δ_limit floor (in the study: box subdivided 50n times). Parallel-friendly; worst sequential record in the 2022 study.
- GL — two-step Pareto: step 1 Pareto-nondominated on (size ↑, f(center) ↓); step 2 Pareto-nondominated on (size ↑, Euclidean distance from x_min ↓); union. No ε, no parameters; "does not have any protection against over-exploration in sub-optimal local minima regions".

** Partitioning schemes
- N-DTC — trisect *all* longest sides at once (2k+1 new evals per POH, k = # of max sides); original DIRECT (Jones 1993).
- 1-DTC — trisect the single longest side only (2 evals per POH); tie-break in the study: least-split-so-far dimension, then lowest index. - 1-DTDV — trisect single longest side, sample two *diagonal vertices*; boundary-optimum weapon; catastrophic on interior optima / high n.

#+TITLE: DIRECT Variant Surface — selection × partitioning × refinement control × hidden constraints
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: direct-variants

* Summary

The papers license a large, well-measured variant surface: three selection schemes (IO/IA/GL) × four partitioning schemes (N-DTC/1-DTC/1-DTDV/1-DBDP), plus refinement-control add-ons (epsilon, delta-limit, median/average, globally-biased, rev) and a hidden-constraint surrogate (DIRECT-GLh). For a 6-DOF search at 20k–35k evaluations, the literature says the current repo configuration — original-DIRECT selection with ε=0 and all ties, 1-DTC partition, L2 size — sits in the worst local-refinement regime; the highest-evidence upgrade is the GL (two-step Pareto) selection combined with 1-DTC or 1-DBDP partitioning, optionally with the globally-biased (-gb) phase switch for refinement control, and the GLh φ = f_min + d(x_min,x) surrogate if unrenderable poses produce NaN. The "restrictions hurt cheap functions" finding (Mathematics 2022, 10, 3760) is real and worse when f_min ≈ 0 (the silhouette-cost shape), and -gb is indeed the only restriction that never hurt in that study — it was also the best on expensive functions. Every variant below can be expressed as an Options struct on DirectOptimizer with bit-identical defaults, and scored headlessly on a DIRECTGOLib/GKLS battery under the production cumulative-budget shape.

* Key Findings

** Finding 1: The repo's current configuration is the literature's worst-case local-refinement regime
- The extracted optimizer is original-DIRECT selection (Jarvis convex hull) with ε=0, selecting *all* hull points including equal-slope ties (`slope >= highest_slope`), trisecting one (largest denormalized) side, L2 size measure (norm of the side vector), center sampling. [Source: /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp L93-141, L143-200; /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/data_structures_6D.cpp L107-128]
- Jones & Martins 2021: "with ε=0 DIRECT spends so many evaluations refining local minima that it ends up far from the optimum after 3000 evaluations" (Shubert); the ε=0 regime allows "excessive local search". The ε|f_min| rule is what protects the original DIRECT from this — the repo has no such rule at all. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 (JOG 79:521–566, DOI 10.1007/s10898-020-00952-6), §3.3/Fig. 19]
- The empirical study's "IO" (improved original) scheme restricts ties to one candidate per (size,value) group; the repo selects all ties, which the study and Jones & Martins show increases "global drag" and slows convergence ("Best results are achieved by ignoring ties for potentially optimal rectangles, only trisecting on one side, and using Gablonsky's modified definition of rectangle size" — Figure 18). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §2.1.1; https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 §3.2]
- Confidence: high (code-verified against primary literature).
- Relevance: the 20k trunk budget is exactly the regime where ε=0 over-refinement wastes evaluations; tie-all selection adds drag on top. Both are cheap to fix (hull tie-break + optional ε filter) with bit-identical defaults preserved.

** Finding 2: GL selection beats IO/IA by ~60–72% on n>4 problems — the regime the 6-DOF search lives in
- On 96 DIRECTGOLib v1.1 box-constrained problems: GL-based variants failed 19/384 cases vs IO 63/384 and IA 55/384; GL required ~60% (vs IO) and ~62% (vs IA) fewer function evaluations overall, and ~72% fewer on n>4 problems. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4.2]
- Budget-regime crossover (operational characteristics, n>4 multimodal): at ≤500 evals IO variants lead; at ~1000–4000 N-DTC-IO is best (~50% solved); at ≥4000 evals the GL variants (1-DTC-GL, 1-DBDP-GL) are the most efficient. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 Fig. 7, §4.2]
- Partitioning for n>4: 1-DBDP-based variants best average (≈16% fewer evals than N-DTC-based); 1-DTDV "very inefficient for higher dimensional test problems"; 1-DTDV shines only when most solution coordinates sit on the boundary (ν≥8/10 coordinates: 551 evals vs 6,487 for N-DTC-IO on Levy10; but 141,999 vs 919 when interior). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4.1, Table 3]
- On 800 GKLS problems (n=2–5, simple+hard classes): 1-DTC-IO best average (8,021) and best median (1,427); 1-DBDP-GL ranks 5th there but is best on simple classes at budgets >400 evals; IO wins on hard GKLS classes. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §5, Table 6]
- Confidence: high (directly from the study's tables; the study is the repo's own evidence base, papers/ 2022 PDF).
- Relevance: 6-DOF = n>4; 20k trunk = well above the 4000-eval crossover → GL selection is the evidence-backed choice; the partition choice is a tradeoff (1-DTC: best GKLS median + minimal change from current code; 1-DBDP: best n>4 average but requires diagonal-bisection rework). 1-DTDV is a trap unless the pose optimum is confirmed near the range boundary.

** Finding 3: The DIRECT-GLh hidden-constraint surrogate is applicable to NaN/unrenderable poses at negligible cost
- GLh assigns infeasible midpoints the surrogate φ = f_min + d(x_min, x) (Euclidean distance in the *normalized unit cube*), normalized via f̄(x)=(f−f_min)/(f_max−f_min) and d̄=d/d_max so objective and distance are commensurate; f̄_min ≡ 0 drops out. Infeasible points never become f_min (min over feasible only). [Source: thesis §5.2, DOI 10.15388/vu.thesis.138 (mif.vu.lt PDF); DIRECTGO code /tmp clone Algorithms/sDirect_GLh.m Selection()]
- Cost is minimal: the distances d(x_min, x) are *already computed* for the GL two-step selection (the local step is Pareto on (size, distance)); per-iteration cost is one O(N) pass to re-tag infeasible values whenever f_min improves. "Such a technique does not require any additional computation." [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 (DIRECTGO, ACM TOMS 48(4), DOI 10.1145/3559755) §2.3; sDirect_GLh.m]

* Variant Surface (12 + refinement add-ons)

** Selection schemes
- IO — Improved Original: lower-right convex hull of (size, f(center)) with ε in eq. (4), ties restricted to one candidate per (size,value) group. Current repo = this *without* ε and *with* all ties.
- IA — Improved Aggressive: select the min-value box of every distinct size group, with δ_limit floor (in the study: box subdivided 50n times). Parallel-friendly; worst sequential record in the 2022 study.
- GL — two-step Pareto: step 1 Pareto-nondominated on (size ↑, f(center) ↓); step 2 Pareto-nondominated on (size ↑, Euclidean distance from x_min ↓); union. No ε, no parameters; "does not have any protection against over-exploration in sub-optimal local minima regions".

** Partitioning schemes
- N-DTC — trisect *all* longest sides at once (2k+1 new evals per POH, k = # of max sides); original DIRECT (Jones 1993).
- 1-DTC — trisect the single longest side only (2 evals per POH); tie-break in the study: least-split-so-far dimension, then lowest index. Repo is 1-DTC-alike but ties break by *denormalized* side length (GetLargestDirection on denormalized sides), lowest index on equality — for anisotropic ranges (branch 15,15,25,25,25,25; leaf 3,3,15,3,3,3) the two rules diverge.
- 1-DTDV — trisect single longest side, sample two *diagonal vertices*; boundary-optimum weapon; catastrophic on interior optima / high n.
- 1-DBDP — bisect along the diagonal, sample two interior diagonal points (reusable across descendants); best n>4 average; needs its own storage/diameter bookkeeping.

** Refinement-control add-ons (on top of GL, per Mathematics 2022)
- -min / -median / -average: ε-style floors f_min−ε|f_min|, f_min−ε|f_min−f_median|, f_min−ε|f_min−f_average| — all hurt, worst at f*=0.
- -limit: δ_limit floor (20n subdivisions in the 2022 paper) + always select the f_min box — hurt slightly (0.7805→0.7631 success).
- -gb: globally-biased two-phase switch (drop local phase after 5 non-improving iterations, security iteration every 5th) — the only non-hurting restriction; best on expensive functions.
- -rev: local phase only on the iteration f_min improves — mixed (best median, 5th success rate).
- ε=0 default in the repo vs ε=1e-4 in DIRECTGO defaults: keep 0 (current behavior) for the analytic battery baseline; the ε>0 option exists for the original-selection regime.

The 1-DTC-GL-gb algorithm switches back to the traditional phase when the f_min value is improved and during 'security' iteration. Finally, we note that the recommended values [10,28] for the additional parameters necessary to switch between phases are used in 1-DTC-GL-gb." #+TITLE: Cost-Path Foundation: 7 Verified Bugs + Metric-Math Test Inventory
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: cost-path-foundation

* Summary

All 7 bugs are confirmed in the current source at the dispatch's line numbers, and all but two are dead for the oracle: only the DistanceMapMetric index bug (distance_map_metric.cu:27) is live in the DIRECT_DILATION cost the oracle evaluates, so the IoU 0.9936 baseline is contaminated by a deterministically-wrong distance-map term; the remaining bugs poison latent paths (DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT UB read + Y_TRANS no-op, sym_trap x→z, always-Trunk stage guard, Mahfouz pointer-guard + int truncation, curvature stub + per-stage allocation leak). The dilation contradiction resolves to code = 6/4/1 (settings_control.cpp:1201-1206 sets branch=4, leaf=1; settings_constants.h 6/−2/1; the 6/3/1 claim lives only in golden_oracle.org prose + baseline.json and is never exercised by the oracle's flat trunk-only budget). The backface divergence is load-bearing for the oracle: the label generator (Study2Grid) renders with culling OFF ("BACKFACE CULLING APPEARS TO BE GIVING ERRORS", main.cpp:277) and the start-pose correspondence is empirically IoU==1.0 only under OFF; production OptimizerManager uses ON. Every bug gets a pin-first recipe: headless Tier-0 where a pure surface exists (transform helpers, index arithmetic, metric semantics as CPU references), Tier-2 GPU-labeled where the pin must observe the cost function itself.

* Key Findings

** Bug 1 — DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:134: uninitialized min_dist (UB read)

- Failure mode: `double min_dist;` is declared uninitialized; the accumulation is +=-only inside `if (x_tran/y_tran/z_tran)` guards; the value is unconditionally read at `return metric_score + min_dist;` (line 159). The registry defaults for all three flags are false (CostFunctionManager.cpp listCostFunctions: X_TRANS/Y_TRANS/Z_TRANS false), so the += never executes and the return reads a fully-indeterminate double — UB ([basic.indet]). In practice the stack residue can be a signalling NaN → cost NaN → DIRECT's comparisons all false → optimizer misbehaves silently. Even with a flag true, += starts from garbage.
- Pin (Tier-0 pure, via extraction): extract the accumulation into a pure helper `double PolePenalty(x_dist, y_dist, z_dist, bool x_t, bool y_t, bool z_t, double weight)` that initializes `min_dist = 0.0` and sums only enabled axes. Spec test: `REQUIRE(PolePenalty(1.0,2.0,3.0,false,false,false,75.0) == 0.0)` (no flags → exactly 0 contribution) and `REQUIRE(PolePenalty(1,2,3,true,false,false,75) == 75.0)`. Today the code has no such pure surface and the cost returns `metric + garbage`, so the spec test fails by construction against the current implementation (cannot link a correct helper, and the Tier-2 variant below observes the garbage).
- Pin (Tier-2 GPU-labeled, fails today): at any fixed pose with PoleWeight=0 and all flags false, `costFunctionDD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT()` must equal `white_sum_A + FastImplantDilationMetric(...)` (the chamfer-only term, computable directly in the test via GPUMetrics). Today the return additionally carries whatever the uninitialized stack slot held. [Source: src/compute/DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:134-159]
- Fix: `double min_dist = 0.0;` (line 134).
- Oracle impact: none — DIRECT_DILATION never calls this function. Confidence: high.

** Bug 2 — DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:117-120: Y_dist ≡ X_dist, Y_TRANS a no-op

- Failure mode: the Y-axis projection reuses the X-axis vector: `y_delX = s_x * Δx; y_delY = s_y * Δy; y_delZ = s_z * Δz;` with Δ = np−p (lines 117-119), byte-identical to the X_dist block (112-115). The Y axis of the non-principal frame is r = R·{0,1,0} = (r_x, r_y, r_z), computed at lines 93-95 and used only for alpha. Consequence: Y_TRANS toggles a duplicate of the X_TRANS term; the y-axis separation between femur and tibia is never penalized. If a user enables Y_TRANS expecting a y constraint, they silently get a double-counted x constraint.
- Pin (Tier-0 pure): with identity rotation (all angles 0): r=(0,1,0), s=(1,0,0), a=(0,0,1); pure y-offset Δ=(0,5,0) gives X_dist=|s·Δ|=0, correct Y_dist=|r·Δ|=5, buggy Y_dist=|s·Δ|=0. Spec test on the extracted PolePenalty: `REQUIRE(PolePenalty(0, 5, 0, false, true, false, 1.0) == 5.0)`. Additionally a pure characterization on the vectors: for any pose where the s and r axes differ, `Y_dist != X_dist` must hold — today they are equal by construction. Tier-2 behavioral pin: at a pose offset purely in the non-principal y direction, toggling Y_TRANS must change the cost by `pole_weight * |r·Δ|`; today it changes nothing (Δ⊥s ⇒ X_dist=0) — fails today. Note the Tier-2 variant must run after Bug 1's fix (else min_dist garbage contaminates the delta).
- Fix: line 117-119 use r_x/r_y/r_z: `double y_delX = r_x * (np.x_location_ - p.x_location_);` etc.
- Oracle impact: none. Confidence: high.

** Bug 3 — CostFunctionManager.cpp:46-48: always-true stage guard collapses every stage to Trunk

- Failure mode: `if (stage_ != Stage::Trunk || stage_ != Stage::Branch || stage_ != Stage::Leaf) stage_ = Stage::Trunk;` is a tautology — no value can equal all three enum members, so the condition is always true and `stage_` is forced to Trunk after any constructor call (the Branch/Leaf constructors at settings_control.cpp:1198-1199 and any future stage-conditional logic). Live consequence today: DIRECT_DILATION_T1 (the only stage_ consumer, DIRECT_DILATION_T1.cpp:64,89) always takes its "trunk" branch and dilates the render to 1 px — its branch/leaf behavior is unreachable. DIRECT_DILATION (the oracle's cost) never reads stage_, so the oracle is unaffected.
- Pin (Tier-0, requires one test-support addition): `CostFunctionManager(Stage)` performs no GPU work in the constructor (only listCostFunctions + pointer-null init, CostFunctionManager.cpp:22-53), so a headless test can construct it and assert the stage is preserved — but `stage_` is private with no accessor (CostFunctionManager.h:147). Add `Stage getStage() const` (pure, behavior-neutral) and pin: `REQUIRE(CostFunctionManager(Stage::Branch).getStage() == Stage::Branch); REQUIRE(CostFunctionManager(Stage::Leaf).getStage() == Stage::Leaf);` — fails today (both return Trunk). Caveat: the test target must compile CostFunctionManager.cpp, which pulls CUDA headers (gpu_metrics.cuh); that is a compile-time CUDA dependency, not a runtime-GPU one — a deliberate, flagged relaxation of the "CUDA-free" headless convention for this one target (or gate the target behind JTML_BUILD_TESTS as usual, since the project already requires the CUDA toolkit to build).
- Fix: `||` → `&&` on line 46 (intent: force Trunk only for invalid values; with a 3-value enum the guard is then dead but harmless — or delete it).
- Oracle impact: none. Confidence: high.

** Bug 4 — sym_trap_function.cpp:104-108: tibia transform x replaced by z

- Failure mode: the tibia transform is built as `create_312_transform(x2tib, p.z_location_, p.y_location_, p.z_location_, p.z_angle_, p.x_angle_, p.y_angle_)` — the x slot receives p.z_location_ and the z slot also receives p.z_location_. The femur call (114-118) is correct. The commented-out reference matrix at lines 91-95 shows the intent (x slot = p.x_location_). Consequence: tibia x-translation is ignored, tibia z-translation is duplicated into the x slot; fem2tib = fem2x·x2tib is corrupted → the varus/valgus angle `vv = asin(fem2tib[2][1])` and the pole distance `shortest_distance` are wrong for any pose with distinct x/z, silently corrupting both penalty terms of sym_trap.
- Pin (Tier-0 pure — genuine R13 pin on the buggy code): the transform helpers are plain CPU functions in a header (create_312_transform / invert_transformation / matmult, include/compute/sym_trap_functionCustomVariables.h:53-150). Replicate the cost's tibia call verbatim and assert the spec:
  #+begin_src cpp
  float x2tib[4][4];
  // verbatim from costFunctionsym_trap_function (pre-fix source truth):
  create_312_transform(x2tib, pose.z, pose.y, pose.z, pose.za, pose.xa, pose.ya);
  REQUIRE(x2tib[0][3] == Approx(pose.x)); // x slot must carry tibia x
  REQUIRE(x2tib[2][3] == Approx(pose.z)); // z slot must carry tibia z
  #+end_src
  With pose = (50, 20, 60, 15, -8, 30): today x2tib[0][3] == 60 (not 50) and the assertion fails; after the fix (pose.x in the x slot) it passes. A second pin builds fem2tib for femur-at-origin / tibia-(10,0,0), identity angles, and asserts the relative translation column equals (10,0,0) — today it is (0,0,0) because x slots received z=0.
- Fix: line 106 first argument `p.x_location_`.
- Oracle impact: none. Confidence: high.

** Bug 5 — distance_map_metric.cu:27: wrong grid→pixel index formula (LIVE in the oracle)

- Failure mode: `int i = (blockIdx.y + gridDim.x + blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;` — the block row must multiply, not add: correct is `(blockIdx.y * gridDim.x + blockIdx.x)`. Concrete failure for a 64×64 crop with threads_per_block=256 (16×16 blocks, gridDim=(4,4)): correct block (bx,by) covers crop rows by*4..by*4+3; the buggy formula maps block (0,0) to i∈[1024,1280) ⇒ rows 16-19 instead of 0-3, block (0,1) to rows 20-23, block (1,0) ALSO to rows 20-23 — crop rows 0-15 are never visited and rows 20-23 are visited by two blocks. The only guard is `orig_loc < width*height` (line 38), so reads stay in-image but at wrong offsets (and for crops smaller than 256·gridDim rows the mapping leaves the crop entirely). Both atomicAdd counters (edge_pixel_count, distance_map_score) therefore accumulate at wrong pixels: the metric `score/(count+0.1)` is deterministic but wrong. Because DIRECT_DILATION calls DistanceMapMetric every evaluation (DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80), the oracle's cost landscape — and hence the IoU 0.9936 measurement — includes this corruption. This is the single bug that directly undermines the baseline.
- Pin (Tier-0 pure): extract the mapping into a pure function `int CropIndexToGlobal(int blockIdxY, int gridDimX, int blockIdxX, int blockDimX, int threadIdxX)` and pin full-coverage invariants over a 64×64 crop (gridDim=(4,4), 256 threads): every crop pixel visited exactly once, none outside [0, cw*ch). The correct formula satisfies; the buggy one fails (enumerate both in the test; the failing assertion documents the bug, the passing one pins the fix). Also a Tier-2 GPU-labeled differential: DistanceMapMetric vs the CPU reference on a small synthetic image with a known edge pattern must agree; today they disagree wherever blockIdx.y > 0.
- Fix: line 27 → `int i = (blockIdx.y * gridDim.x + blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;` (this matches the pattern already correct in every other metric kernel, e.g. iou.cu:37, l_1_1_matrix_diff_norm.cu:24, fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:129).
- Oracle impact: HIGH — changes the distance-map term of every oracle cost evaluation; expect the recovered pose / IoU / L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap to move. Must be followed by an oracle re-run and a baseline.json re-baseline (measured IoU 0.9936, per-px L1 0.0207 are informational, gate is IoU > 0.85). Confidence: high.

** Bug 6 — implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:324/446 pointer guard + :93/122 double→int truncation

- Failure mode (guard): `if (pixel_score_ != 0) intensity_score = intensity_score / static_cast<double>(pixel_score_[0]);` (324) and the same at 446 for contour_score — `pixel_score_` is host-pinned memory allocated once in the GPUMetrics constructor (gpu_metrics.cu ctor cudaHostAlloc), so the pointer is never null and the guard always passes; when the denominator kernel counts zero pixels (e.g. an extreme pose with an empty silhouette crop during DIRECT exploration), the division is by 0 → ±inf/NaN cost. The intent was a value check `pixel_score_[0] != 0`.
- Failure mode (truncation): `atomicAdd(&result[0], 2.55 * pixel)` at 93 (EdgeMahfouzNumerator) and 122 (EdgeMahfouzDenominator) — `result` is `int*`, and atomicAdd(int*, int) converts the double 2.55·pixel to int with truncation toward zero (per-pixel error up to 2.55). Both the contour numerator and denominator are quantized, biasing the ratio; the intensity branch (line 153) is integer-valued already, so it is unaffected. The host then multiplies the contour numerator by 255.0 (line ~420) while the kernels' internal scale is 2.55 — a scale inconsistency that should be pinned as current spec (kernel-as-spec) and reconciled against the Mahfouz 2003 paper before "fixing".
- Pins: Tier-0 CPU reference replicates both accumulation semantics on small synthetic images — (a) the intended float/double accumulation of 2.55·pixel vs (b) the actual int-truncated accumulation, asserting they differ (documents the quantization as current behavior); Tier-2 GPU-labeled: with a rendered image whose bbox crop contains no qualifying pixels (denominator 0), `ImplantMahfouzMetric` must return a finite value (guard works) — today it can return ±inf.
- Fix: `if (pixel_score_[0] != 0)` at 324 and 446 (unambiguous bug). Truncation: default to keep-and-pin (kernel-as-spec) unless the Mahfouz paper dictates float accumulation, in which case switch the accumulators to float/double and the CPU reference becomes the spec test. Also note the final combination `contour_score * (-2.67) + intensity_score * (-1)` (line ~465) is an unnormalized weighted sum — pin as-is.
- Oracle impact: none (DIRECT_MAHFOUZ is not the oracle's cost; DIRECT_MAHFOUZ.cpp:38,50 are its only consumers). Confidence: high.

** Bug 7 — curvature_hausdorf_metric.cu: stub returning 0, plus a per-stage-init allocation leak

- Failure mode: CurvatureHausdorfMetric_Kernel (lines 17-38) computes `kp_loc` and then does nothing; the host CurvatureHeatmapMetric launches only Reset_CurvatureHausdorfScoreKernel, computes an unused `double test = 0`, and `return test;` (line 48) — constant 0.0, never reading the heatmaps, never copying dev_curvature_hausdorf_score_ back. Additional defects: crop width off-by-one `right_x - left_x - 1` (line 63, should be +1). Not registered in listCostFunctions, not called by any cost function — latent. The only live seam is initializeDIRECT_DILATION calling AllocateCurvatureHausdorfScore every stage init (DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:42,49), which cudaMalloc/cudaHostAlloc's new buffers each call without freeing the previous ones (gpu_metrics.cu:97-111) — a per-stage-init GPU+host memory leak in the oracle's own setup path, plus an unconditional curvature-heatmap upload in the oracle pipeline (oracle_test.cpp BuildFramePipeline).
- Pin: trivial characterization — `CurvatureHeatmapMetric` returns exactly 0.0 for any input (passes today; documents the stub). The substantive pin is the leak: a GPU-labeled test that calls InitializeActiveCostFunction twice and asserts device-memory growth is bounded (or asserts cudaMalloc is not re-invoked); simpler and headless-friendly: a code-level pin (grep-style) is weak, so recommend the disposition below over a behavioral pin.
- Disposition: explicitly DE-SCOPE, don't implement. Evidence: not registered, never called, semantics undefined ("min distance to keypoints" was never specified), the only wiring is a leaky allocation + a dead upload. Cheapest safe action: (a) remove the AllocateCurvatureHausdorfScore call from initializeDIRECT_DILATION (fixes the per-stage leak, zero cost-value change), (b) add an explicit "DE-SCOPED: stub, not implemented, do not wire into a cost" banner to curvature_hausdorf_metric.cu and gpu_metrics.cuh, (c) leave the kernel body as a starting point if a curvature leaf-cost is ever wanted (it would need a real distance-to-keypoint reduction + a CPU reference first). Implementing it now without a spec would enshrine guesswork into the cost path.
- Oracle impact: (a) removes a per-stage cudaMalloc/cudaHostAlloc from setup; cost values unchanged. Confidence: high.

** Dead duplicate — DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:101-104: delete it

- The commented-out DistanceMapMetric call (lines 101-104) is a byte-identical duplicate of the active monoplane call at line 80 (`gpu_metrics_->DistanceMapMetric(gpu_principal_model_->GetPrimaryCameraRenderedImage(), gpu_distance_maps_->at(current_frame_index_), DIRECT_DILATION_current_dilation_parameter)`). It is dead code and a documented source of confusion (prior angle 01 flagged it). Disposition: delete the four comment lines; zero behavior change; no pin needed beyond "no dead commented calls in the cost path" (optionally a trivial grep-style CI check). Confidence: high.

** Metric-math CPU-reference test inventory (Tier-0, headless; feeds 03's harness)

Where the math is ambiguous the CURRENT KERNEL CODE is the spec; the CPU references below encode that spec so future kernel changes are diffable. File targets: new test/unit/test_metric_semantics.cpp (+ hegel twin test_metric_semantics_properties.cpp) registered as explicit .cpp-list targets in test/CMakeLists.txt (jtml_test_metric_semantics / jtml_test_metric_semantics_props, headless label, mirroring the house pattern at test/CMakeLists.txt:239-276). The GPU-vs-CPU differential comparisons belong to 03's harness (oracle label); the Tier-0 files define the reference values it compares against.

- Chamfer — FastImplantDilationMetric (src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu): semantics to pin: (a) edge detection = 8-neighbor boundary of WHITE(255) against BLACK(0) → EDGE(100), interior/exterior untouched; (b) dilation = for each EDGE pixel, offsets (±j, ±k) with j,k ∈ [1, dilation] write DILATED(99) only over WHITE/BLACK pixels — EDGE and already-DILATED pixels are never overwritten, and the axial cross (j=0 or k=0) is never dilated (quadrant-only morphology — spec quirk, verified in DilateKernel lines 83-118); (c) difference = +1 per dilated/edge pixel where comparison==WHITE(255), −1 otherwise (lines 120-145); (d) return −1·score; (e) cost composition = comparison_white_sum + chamfer ⇒ 0 at perfect overlap; (f) NO normalization — the chamfer term is absolute pixel counts, so its weight scales with silhouette size (relevant for the z-sensitivity analysis: this is the only z-sensitive term per the synthesis). Pin each stage as a pure function over small uchar images (32×32, 64×64) plus the composed minimum-at-match property.
- Distance map — DistanceMapMetric (src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu): semantics to pin: sum of distance_map values at pixels where projected_image == EDGE(100) within the bbox±dilation crop, divided by (count + 0.1) (the +0.1 singularity hack distorts low-count cases — pin it as spec, flag for review); the crop grid mapping must use the CORRECTED index formula (Bug 5); and the composition quirk: the input buffer arrives already mutated by FastImplantDilationMetric (edge/dilated values in place), so only the surviving EDGE(100) ring is sampled — DILATED(99) pixels are not counted (kernel line 34: `projected_image[orig_loc] == EDGE_PIXEL`).
- Mahfouz ratios — ImplantMahfouzMetric (src/compute/implant_mahfouz_metric.cu): intensity ratio = Σ(comparison-white-silhouette intensity · rendered-white) / Σ(rendered-white) (kernels 129-155, guard bug at 324); contour ratio with the 2.55·pixel int-truncation (93/122) and the host's 255.0 scale + final −2.67·contour − intensity (line ~465). Pin both the intended float math and the actual truncated math; assert they differ; document the scale chain.
- IoU — IOU (src/compute/iou.cu): intersection/union over the UNION of the two bounding boxes, pixel-nonzero criterion (A>0 || B>0), not ==255; IoU(A,A)=1 for non-empty A; region-restricted (pixels outside both bboxes excluded). Trivial CPU reference; PBT properties: range [0,1], symmetry, reflexivity.
- L1 — L_1_1_MatrixDifferenceNorm (src/compute/l_1_1_matrix_diff_norm.cu): Σ|A−B| over the union-bbox crop (NOT the full frame); PBT properties: symmetry, L1(A,A)=0, non-negativity.
- ComputeSumWhitePixels (src/compute/gpu_metrics.cu:134): count of pixels == WHITE(255).
- PBT invariants for the hegel twin: IoU ∈ [0,1]; IoU(A,B)=IoU(B,A); IoU(A,A)=1; L1(A,B)=L1(B,A); L1(A,A)=0; chamfer(A,A)=0 after adding the comparison white sum; distance-map score ≥ 0; Mahfouz ratios ≥ 0. Use small synthetic uchar images (sampled 16×16 / 32×32), mirroring the typed round-trip PBT style in test_cost_function_properties.cpp.

** Dilation 6/4/1 vs 6/3/1 — resolution with evidence

- The code implements 6/4/1: settings_control.cpp:1201-1206 explicitly sets branch DIRECT_DILATION Dilation=4 and leaf Dilation=1 ("Change the Default Settings of Dilation for branch and leaf to 4 and 1 respectively"); trunk stays at the registry default 6 (CostFunctionManager.cpp listCostFunctions: DIRECT_DILATION Dilation=6). settings_constants.h TRUNK_DILATION=6 / BRANCH_DILATION_DECREASE=2 / Z_SEARCH_DILATION=1 agree with 6/4/1 but are consumed ONLY by the experimental SettingsBridge (src/app/experimental/SettingsBridge.cpp:406,412 + experimental_settings_test) — production OptimizerManager never reads them; it reads the per-manager "Dilation" runtime parameter instead (optimizer_manager.cpp:235-289), with a hardcoded override to 3 only for DIRECT_MAHFOUZ.
- The 6/3/1 claim lives only in golden_oracle.org prose ("trunk is 6px dilated, branch is 3px dilated, leaf is 1px dilated", marked "(confirmed)") and baseline.json dilation_px {6,3,1}. The oracle itself never exercises branch or leaf (flat budget 3000, single trunk DIRECT_DILATION stage, oracle_test.cpp kBudget=3000), so neither claim was ever measured by the Tier-2 gate.
- Both claims agree on trunk 6 and leaf 1; the conflict is branch only (4 vs 3).
- Resolution path (per the run owner's "resolve, don't assume"): (1) pin the code-as-spec with a Tier-0 registry test: DIRECT_DILATION default Dilation == 6 (already testable via CostFunction.cpp, extend test_cost_function.cpp) plus a constants test pinning TRUNK_DILATION=6, BRANCH_DILATION_DECREASE=2, Z_SEARCH_DILATION=1; (2) a runtime probe (03's harness territory) reading the three managers' Dilation params after settings_control-style construction — expect 6/4/1; (3) then either update golden_oracle.org + baseline.json to 6/4/1 (if 4 is intended) or change settings_control.cpp:1204 to 3 + update settings_constants comment (if the JTA-paper-style 6/3/1 is intended). My source evidence favors 6/4/1 as the implemented intent; the docs are the stale artifact. Confidence: high on "code = 6/4/1"; medium on which value is intended.

** Backface divergence — reconciliation with evidence

- Production: monoplane OptimizerManager constructs GPUModel with use_backface_culling=true (optimizer_manager.cpp:716,721 — 6th constructor arg true); biplane true/true (765,788). Oracle/parity paths all use false: oracle_test.cpp:207, qml_parity_check.cpp:238, segmentation_oracle_test.cpp:173, MlBridge.cpp:336.
- Label generator: Study2Grid uses false with the in-source comment "BACKFACE CULLING APPEARS TO BE GIVING ERRORS" (src/app/Study2Grid/main.cpp:263-277).
- Renderer mechanics: there is no z-buffer — backface triangles get zero rasterization size (BoundingBoxSizesKernel skips dev_backface[i]==true, render_engine.cu:534-566) and the fill is a point-in-triangle shade (FillTriangleKernel, render_engine.cu:616+). So culling OFF paints front AND back faces; for a closed manifold viewed from outside the outlines coincide (back faces project inside the front outline), but for concave/self-occluding geometry (femoral condyle undercuts) or an OPEN segmentation-derived STL, culling ON can drop visible pixels and change the silhouette boundary.
- Which is correct for the appearance oracle: OFF, and it is load-bearing. The labels were generated with OFF (Study2Grid), and the oracle's frame↔label correspondence is pinned EMPIRICALLY by start-pose render IoU == 1.0 (oracle_test.cpp diagnostic + golden_oracle.org/baseline.json) — that correspondence only holds under the same OFF convention. Switching the oracle to ON would change the rendered silhouette where the STL is open/concave and break the gate against OFF-generated labels. The measured 0.9936 is an OFF-vs-OFF number and is self-consistent.
- For production (ON): defensible for a closed opaque implant fitting real x-rays, but it renders a different silhouette convention than the labels. Recommended evidence before deciding: (a) headless STL manifoldness check on KR_right_7_fem.stl (count boundary edges: closed ⇒ 0), (b) GPU-labeled ON-vs-OFF silhouette IoU at the golden pose: ≈1.0 ⇒ the divergence is immaterial for this model and production ON can stay; measurably < 1 ⇒ production and the oracle render different silhouettes and the two paths must be reconciled deliberately (either both OFF to match the label convention, or regenerate labels under ON). My recommendation: keep the oracle OFF (pinned), run the two evidence checks, and only then touch production. Confidence: high on "oracle must stay OFF"; medium on the production-correct answer until the checks run.

** Fix order (cheapest-first; only Bug 5 moves the oracle)

- Phase 0 — pins only (no behavior change): all Tier-0 pins above (stage-guard accessor + pin; DD PolePenalty extraction + init-0/Y-axis pins; sym_trap tibia-transform pin; distance-map index-mapping pin; metric-semantics CPU references + PBT twin; dilation constants/registry pins). All red or spec-documenting. This is the R13 characterization pass; it also creates the pure surfaces the fixes plug into.
- Phase 1 — behavior-neutral fixes (cannot move oracle numbers; none touch the DIRECT_DILATION path): (1) CostFunctionManager.cpp:46 ||→&& (+ getStage accessor); (2) DD min_dist init (line 134); (3) DD Y-axis vector (117-119); (4) sym_trap tibia x→z (line 106); (5) delete DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:101-104 dead block. One commit each, jj per logical change.
- Phase 2 — the live one: (6) distance_map_metric.cu:27 index fix; immediately re-run the Tier-2 oracle and RE-BASELINE baseline.json (IoU gate 0.85 unchanged; measured IoU/L1/z-gap are informational and expected to move; the 6.31 mm z gap is the number most likely to change since the distance-map term is the z-sensitive complement of the chamfer). #+TITLE: Cost-Path Foundation: 7 Verified Bugs + Metric-Math Test Inventory
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: cost-path-foundation

* Summary

All 7 bugs are confirmed in the current source at the dispatch's line numbers, and all but two are dead for the oracle: only the DistanceMapMetric index bug (distance_map_metric.cu:27) is live in the DIRECT_DILATION cost the oracle evaluates, so the IoU 0.9936 baseline is contaminated by a deterministically-wrong distance-map term; the remaining bugs poison latent paths (DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT UB read + Y_TRANS no-op, sym_trap x→z, always-Trunk stage guard, Mahfouz pointer-guard + int truncation, curvature stub + per-stage allocation leak). The dilation contradiction resolves to code = 6/4/1 (settings_control.cpp:1201-1206 sets branch=4, leaf=1; settings_constants.h 6/−2/1; the 6/3/1 claim lives only in golden_oracle.org prose + baseline.json and is never exercised by the oracle's flat trunk-only budget). The backface divergence is load-bearing for the oracle: the label generator (Study2Grid) renders with culling OFF ("BACKFACE CULLING APPEARS TO BE GIVING ERRORS", main.cpp:277) and the start-pose correspondence is empirically IoU==1.0 only under OFF; production OptimizerManager uses ON. Every bug gets a pin-first recipe: headless Tier-0 where a pure surface exists (transform helpers, index arithmetic, metric semantics as CPU references), Tier-2 GPU-labeled where the pin must observe the cost function itself.

* Key Findings

** Bug 1 — DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:134: uninitialized min_dist (UB read)

- Failure mode: `double min_dist;` is declared uninitialized; the accumulation is +=-only inside `if (x_tran/y_tran/z_tran)` guards; the value is unconditionally read at `return metric_score + min_dist;` (line 159). The registry defaults for all three flags are false (CostFunctionManager.cpp listCostFunctions: X_TRANS/Y_TRANS/Z_TRANS false), so the += never executes and the return reads a fully-indeterminate double — UB ([basic.indet]). In practice the stack residue can be a signalling NaN → cost NaN → DIRECT's comparisons all false → optimizer misbehaves silently. Even with a flag true, += starts from garbage.
- Pin (Tier-0 pure, via extraction): extract the accumulation into a pure helper `double PolePenalty(x_dist, y_dist, z_dist, bool x_t, bool y_t, bool z_t, double weight)` that initializes `min_dist = 0.0` and sums only enabled axes. Spec test: `REQUIRE(PolePenalty(1.0,2.0,3.0,false,false,false,75.0) == 0.0)` (no flags → exactly 0 contribution) and `REQUIRE(PolePenalty(1,2,3,true,false,false,75) == 75.0)`. Today the code has no such pure surface and the cost returns `metric + garbage`, so the spec test fails by construction against the current implementation (cannot link a correct helper, and the Tier-2 variant below observes the garbage).
- Pin (Tier-2 GPU-labeled, fails today): at any fixed pose with PoleWeight=0 and all flags false, `costFunctionDD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT()` must equal `white_sum_A + FastImplantDilationMetric(...)` (the chamfer-only term, computable directly in the test via GPUMetrics). Today the return additionally carries whatever the uninitialized stack slot held. [Source: src/compute/DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:134-159]
- Fix: `double min_dist = 0.0;` (line 134).
- Oracle impact: none — DIRECT_DILATION never calls this function. Confidence: high.

** Bug 2 — DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:117-120: Y_dist ≡ X_dist, Y_TRANS a no-op

- Failure mode: the Y-axis projection reuses the X-axis vector: `y_delX = s_x * Δx; y_delY = s_y * Δy; y_delZ = s_z * Δz;` with Δ = np−p (lines 117-119), byte-identical to the X_dist block (112-115). The Y axis of the non-principal frame is r = R·{0,1,0} = (r_x, r_y, r_z), computed at lines 93-95 and used only for alpha. Consequence: Y_TRANS toggles a duplicate of the X_TRANS term; the y-axis separation between femur and tibia is never penalized. If a user enables Y_TRANS expecting a y constraint, they silently get a double-counted x constraint.
- Pin (Tier-0 pure): with identity rotation (all angles 0): r=(0,1,0), s=(1,0,0), a=(0,0,1); pure y-offset Δ=(0,5,0) gives X_dist=|s·Δ|=0, correct Y_dist=|r·Δ|=5, buggy Y_dist=|s·Δ|=0. Spec test on the extracted PolePenalty: `REQUIRE(PolePenalty(0, 5, 0, false, true, false, 1.0) == 5.0)`. Additionally a pure characterization on the vectors: for any pose where the s and r axes differ, `Y_dist != X_dist` must hold — today they are equal by construction. Tier-2 behavioral pin: at a pose offset purely in the non-principal y direction, toggling Y_TRANS must change the cost by `pole_weight * |r·Δ|`; today it changes nothing (Δ⊥s ⇒ X_dist=0) — fails today. Note the Tier-2 variant must run after Bug 1's fix (else min_dist garbage contaminates the delta).
- Fix: line 117-119 use r_x/r_y/r_z: `double y_delX = r_x * (np.x_location_ - p.x_location_);` etc.
- Oracle impact: none. Confidence: high.

** Bug 3 — CostFunctionManager.cpp:46-48: always-true stage guard collapses every stage to Trunk

- Failure mode: `if (stage_ != Stage::Trunk || stage_ != Stage::Branch || stage_ != Stage::Leaf) stage_ = Stage::Trunk;` is a tautology — no value can equal all three enum members, so the condition is always true and `stage_` is forced to Trunk after any constructor call (the Branch/Leaf constructors at settings_control.cpp:1198-1199 and any future stage-conditional logic). Live consequence today: DIRECT_DILATION_T1 (the only stage_ consumer, DIRECT_DILATION_T1.cpp:64,89) always takes its "trunk" branch and dilates the render to 1 px — its branch/leaf behavior is unreachable. DIRECT_DILATION (the oracle's cost) never reads stage_, so the oracle is unaffected.
- Pin (Tier-0, requires one test-support addition): `CostFunctionManager(Stage)` performs no GPU work in the constructor (only listCostFunctions + pointer-null init, CostFunctionManager.cpp:22-53), so a headless test can construct it and assert the stage is preserved — but `stage_` is private with no accessor (CostFunctionManager.h:147). Add `Stage getStage() const` (pure, behavior-neutral) and pin: `REQUIRE(CostFunctionManager(Stage::Branch).getStage() == Stage::Branch); REQUIRE(CostFunctionManager(Stage::Leaf).getStage() == Stage::Leaf);` — fails today (both return Trunk). Caveat: the test target must compile CostFunctionManager.cpp, which pulls CUDA headers (gpu_metrics.cuh); that is a compile-time CUDA dependency, not a runtime-GPU one — a deliberate, flagged relaxation of the "CUDA-free" headless convention for this one target (or gate the target behind JTML_BUILD_TESTS as usual, since the project already requires the CUDA toolkit to build).
- Fix: `||` → `&&` on line 46 (intent: force Trunk only for invalid values; with a 3-value enum the guard is then dead but harmless — or delete it).
- Oracle impact: none. Confidence: high.

** Bug 4 — sym_trap_function.cpp:104-108: tibia transform x replaced by z

- Failure mode: the tibia transform is built as `create_312_transform(x2tib, p.z_location_, p.y_location_, p.z_location_, p.z_angle_, p.x_angle_, p.y_angle_)` — the x slot receives p.z_location_ and the z slot also receives p.z_location_. The femur call (114-118) is correct. The commented-out reference matrix at lines 91-95 shows the intent (x slot = p.x_location_). Consequence: tibia x-translation is ignored, tibia z-translation is duplicated into the x slot; fem2tib = fem2x·x2tib is corrupted → the varus/valgus angle `vv = asin(fem2tib[2][1])` and the pole distance `shortest_distance` are wrong for any pose with distinct x/z, silently corrupting both penalty terms of sym_trap.
- Pin (Tier-0 pure — genuine R13 pin on the buggy code): the transform helpers are plain CPU functions in a header (create_312_transform / invert_transformation / matmult, include/compute/sym_trap_functionCustomVariables.h:53-150). Replicate the cost's tibia call verbatim and assert the spec:
  #+begin_src cpp
  float x2tib[4][4];
  // verbatim from costFunctionsym_trap_function (pre-fix source truth):
  create_312_transform(x2tib, pose.z, pose.y, pose.z, pose.za, pose.xa, pose.ya);
  REQUIRE(x2tib[0][3] == Approx(pose.x)); // x slot must carry tibia x
  REQUIRE(x2tib[2][3] == Approx(pose.z)); // z slot must carry tibia z
  #+end_src
  With pose = (50, 20, 60, 15, -8, 30): today x2tib[0][3] == 60 (not 50) and the assertion fails; after the fix (pose.x in the x slot) it passes. A second pin builds fem2tib for femur-at-origin / tibia-(10,0,0), identity angles, and asserts the relative translation column equals (10,0,0) — today it is (0,0,0) because x slots received z=0.
- Fix: line 106 first argument `p.x_location_`.
- Oracle impact: none. Confidence: high.

** Bug 5 — distance_map_metric.cu:27: wrong grid→pixel index formula (LIVE in the oracle)

- Failure mode: `int i = (blockIdx.y + gridDim.x + blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;` — the block row must multiply, not add: correct is `(blockIdx.y * gridDim.x + blockIdx.x)`. Concrete failure for a 64×64 crop with threads_per_block=256 (16×16 blocks, gridDim=(4,4)): correct block (bx,by) covers crop rows by*4..by*4+3; the buggy formula maps block (0,0) to i∈[1024,1280) ⇒ rows 16-19 instead of 0-3, block (0,1) to rows 20-23, block (1,0) ALSO to rows 20-23 — crop rows 0-15 are never visited and rows 20-23 are visited by two blocks. The only guard is `orig_loc < width*height` (line 38), so reads stay in-image but at wrong offsets (and for crops smaller than 256·gridDim rows the mapping leaves the crop entirely). Both atomicAdd counters (edge_pixel_count, distance_map_score) therefore accumulate at wrong pixels: the metric `score/(count+0.1)` is deterministic but wrong. Because DIRECT_DILATION calls DistanceMapMetric every evaluation (DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80), the oracle's cost landscape — and hence the IoU 0.9936 measurement — includes this corruption. This is the single bug that directly undermines the baseline.
- Pin (Tier-0 pure): extract the mapping into a pure function `int CropIndexToGlobal(int blockIdxY, int gridDimX, int blockIdxX, int blockDimX, int threadIdxX)` and pin full-coverage invariants over a 64×64 crop (gridDim=(4,4), 256 threads): every crop pixel visited exactly once, none outside [0, cw*ch). The correct formula satisfies; the buggy one fails (enumerate both in the test; the failing assertion documents the bug, the passing one pins the fix). Also a Tier-2 GPU-labeled differential: DistanceMapMetric vs the CPU reference on a small synthetic image with a known edge pattern must agree; today they disagree wherever blockIdx.y > 0.
- Fix: line 27 → `int i = (blockIdx.y * gridDim.x + blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;` (this matches the pattern already correct in every other metric kernel, e.g. iou.cu:37, l_1_1_matrix_diff_norm.cu:24, fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:129).
- Oracle impact: HIGH — changes the distance-map term of every oracle cost evaluation; expect the recovered pose / IoU / L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap to move. Must be followed by an oracle re-run and a baseline.json re-baseline (measured IoU 0.9936, per-px L1 0.0207 are informational, gate is IoU > 0.85). Confidence: high.

** Bug 6 — implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:324/446 pointer guard + :93/122 double→int truncation

- Failure mode (guard): `if (pixel_score_ != 0) intensity_score = intensity_score / static_cast<double>(pixel_score_[0]);` (324) and the same at 446 for contour_score — `pixel_score_` is host-pinned memory allocated once in the GPUMetrics constructor (gpu_metrics.cu ctor cudaHostAlloc), so the pointer is never null and the guard always passes; when the denominator kernel counts zero pixels (e.g. an extreme pose with an empty silhouette crop during DIRECT exploration), the division is by 0 → ±inf/NaN cost. The intent was a value check `pixel_score_[0] != 0`.
- Failure mode (truncation): `atomicAdd(&result[0], 2.55 * pixel)` at 93 (EdgeMahfouzNumerator) and 122 (EdgeMahfouzDenominator) — `result` is `int*`, and atomicAdd(int*, int) converts the double 2.55·pixel to int with truncation toward zero (per-pixel error up to 2.55). Both the contour numerator and denominator are quantized, biasing the ratio; the intensity branch (line 153) is integer-valued already, so it is unaffected. The host then multiplies the contour numerator by 255.0 (line ~420) while the kernels' internal scale is 2.55 — a scale inconsistency that should be pinned as current spec (kernel-as-spec) and reconciled against the Mahfouz 2003 paper before "fixing".
- Pins: Tier-0 CPU reference replicates both accumulation semantics on small synthetic images — (a) the intended float/double accumulation of 2.55·pixel vs (b) the actual int-truncated accumulation, asserting they differ (documents the quantization as current behavior); Tier-2 GPU-labeled: with a rendered image whose bbox crop contains no qualifying pixels (denominator 0), `ImplantMahfouzMetric` must return a finite value (guard works) — today it can return ±inf.
- Fix: `if (pixel_score_[0] != 0)` at 324 and 446 (unambiguous bug). Truncation: default to keep-and-pin (kernel-as-spec) unless the Mahfouz paper dictates float accumulation, in which case switch the accumulators to float/double and the CPU reference becomes the spec test. Also note the final combination `contour_score * (-2.67) + intensity_score * (-1)` (line ~465) is an unnormalized weighted sum — pin as-is.
- Oracle impact: none (DIRECT_MAHFOUZ is not the oracle's cost; DIRECT_MAHFOUZ.cpp:38,50 are its only consumers). Confidence: high.

** Bug 7 — curvature_hausdorf_metric.cu: stub returning 0, plus a per-stage-init allocation leak

- Failure mode: CurvatureHausdorfMetric_Kernel (lines 17-38) computes `kp_loc` and then does nothing; the host CurvatureHeatmapMetric launches only Reset_CurvatureHausdorfScoreKernel, computes an unused `double test = 0`, and `return test;` (line 48) — constant 0.0, never reading the heatmaps, never copying dev_curvature_hausdorf_score_ back. Additional defects: crop width off-by-one `right_x - left_x - 1` (line 63, should be +1). Not registered in listCostFunctions, not called by any cost function — latent. The only live seam is initializeDIRECT_DILATION calling AllocateCurvatureHausdorfScore every stage init (DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:42,49), which cudaMalloc/cudaHostAlloc's new buffers each call without freeing the previous ones (gpu_metrics.cu:97-111) — a per-stage-init GPU+host memory leak in the oracle's own setup path, plus an unconditional curvature-heatmap upload in the oracle pipeline (oracle_test.cpp BuildFramePipeline).
- Pin: trivial characterization — `CurvatureHeatmapMetric` returns exactly 0.0 for any input (passes today; documents the stub). The substantive pin is the leak: a GPU-labeled test that calls InitializeActiveCostFunction twice and asserts device-memory growth is bounded (or asserts cudaMalloc is not re-invoked); simpler and headless-friendly: a code-level pin (grep-style) is weak, so recommend the disposition below over a behavioral pin.
- Disposition: explicitly DE-SCOPE, don't implement. Evidence: not registered, never called, semantics undefined ("min distance to keypoints" was never specified), the only wiring is a leaky allocation + a dead upload. Cheapest safe action: (a) remove the AllocateCurvatureHausdorfScore call from initializeDIRECT_DILATION (fixes the per-stage leak, zero cost-value change), (b) add an explicit "DE-SCOPED: stub, not implemented, do not wire into a cost" banner to curvature_hausdorf_metric.cu and gpu_metrics.cuh, (c) leave the kernel body as a starting point if a curvature leaf-cost is ever wanted (it would need a real distance-to-keypoint reduction + a CPU reference first). Implementing it now without a spec would enshrine guesswork into the cost path.
- Oracle impact: (a) removes a per-stage cudaMalloc/cudaHostAlloc from setup; cost values unchanged. Confidence: high.

** Dead duplicate — DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:101-104: delete it

- The commented-out DistanceMapMetric call (lines 101-104) is a byte-identical duplicate of the active monoplane call at line 80 (`gpu_metrics_->DistanceMapMetric(gpu_principal_model_->GetPrimaryCameraRenderedImage(), gpu_distance_maps_->at(current_frame_index_), DIRECT_DILATION_current_dilation_parameter)`). It is dead code and a documented source of confusion (prior angle 01 flagged it). Disposition: delete the four comment lines; zero behavior change; no pin needed beyond "no dead commented calls in the cost path" (optionally a trivial grep-style CI check). Confidence: high.

** Metric-math CPU-reference test inventory (Tier-0, headless; feeds 03's harness)

Where the math is ambiguous the CURRENT KERNEL CODE is the spec; the CPU references below encode that spec so future kernel changes are diffable. File targets: new test/unit/test_metric_semantics.cpp (+ hegel twin test_metric_semantics_properties.cpp) registered as explicit .cpp-list targets in test/CMakeLists.txt (jtml_test_metric_semantics / jtml_test_metric_semantics_props, headless label, mirroring the house pattern at test/CMakeLists.txt:239-276). The GPU-vs-CPU differential comparisons belong to 03's harness (oracle label); the Tier-0 files define the reference values it compares against.

- Chamfer — FastImplantDilationMetric (src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu): semantics to pin: (a) edge detection = 8-neighbor boundary of WHITE(255) against BLACK(0) → EDGE(100), interior/exterior untouched; (b) dilation = for each EDGE pixel, offsets (±j, ±k) with j,k ∈ [1, dilation] write DILATED(99) only over WHITE/BLACK pixels — EDGE and already-DILATED pixels are never overwritten, and the axial cross (j=0 or k=0) is never dilated (quadrant-only morphology — spec quirk, verified in DilateKernel lines 83-118); (c) difference = +1 per dilated/edge pixel where comparison==WHITE(255), −1 otherwise (lines 120-145); (d) return −1·score; (e) cost composition = comparison_white_sum + chamfer ⇒ 0 at perfect overlap; (f) NO normalization — the chamfer term is absolute pixel counts, so its weight scales with silhouette size (relevant for the z-sensitivity analysis: this is the only z-sensitive term per the synthesis). Pin each stage as a pure function over small uchar images (32×32, 64×64) plus the composed minimum-at-match property.
- Distance map — DistanceMapMetric (src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu): semantics to pin: sum of distance_map values at pixels where projected_image == EDGE(100) within the bbox±dilation crop, divided by (count + 0.1) (the +0.1 singularity hack distorts low-count cases — pin it as spec, flag for review); the crop grid mapping must use the CORRECTED index formula (Bug 5); and the composition quirk: the input buffer arrives already mutated by FastImplantDilationMetric (edge/dilated values in place), so only the surviving EDGE(100) ring is sampled — DILATED(99) pixels are not counted (kernel line 34: `projected_image[orig_loc] == EDGE_PIXEL`).
- Mahfouz ratios — ImplantMahfouzMetric (src/compute/implant_mahfouz_metric.cu): intensity ratio = Σ(comparison-white-silhouette intensity · rendered-white) / Σ(rendered-white) (kernels 129-155, guard bug at 324); contour ratio with the 2.55·pixel int-truncation (93/122) and the host's 255.0 scale + final −2.67·contour − intensity (line ~465). Pin both the intended float math and the actual truncated math; assert they differ; document the scale chain.
- IoU — IOU (src/compute/iou.cu): intersection/union over the UNION of the two bounding boxes, pixel-nonzero criterion (A>0 || B>0), not ==255; IoU(A,A)=1 for non-empty A; region-restricted (pixels outside both bboxes excluded). Trivial CPU reference; PBT properties: range [0,1], symmetry, reflexivity.
- L1 — L_1_1_MatrixDifferenceNorm (src/compute/l_1_1_matrix_diff_norm.cu): Σ|A−B| over the union-bbox crop (NOT the full frame); PBT properties: symmetry, L1(A,A)=0, non-negativity.
- ComputeSumWhitePixels (src/compute/gpu_metrics.cu:134): count of pixels == WHITE(255).
- PBT invariants for the hegel twin: IoU ∈ [0,1]; IoU(A,B)=IoU(B,A); IoU(A,A)=1; L1(A,B)=L1(B,A); L1(A,A)=0; chamfer(A,A)=0 after adding the comparison white sum; distance-map score ≥ 0; Mahfouz ratios ≥ 0.
