#+TITLE: Compute Performance of the GPU Cost Path — Sync-Point Inventory, Streamed Pipeline, Instrumentation, Ordered Cuts
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: compute-perf

* Summary

The synthesis item-8 claim (cost path is sync-bound, not kernel-bound) is *directionally confirmed by source structure but not yet measured*: every eval runs on the default stream with zero streams/events anywhere in src/, and 5 synchronous `cudaMemcpy` D2H calls per monoplane eval (`render_engine.cu:781-790` ×2, `fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:289-290` ×1, `distance_map_metric.cu:110-119` ×2) each drain the entire device pipeline, leaving the GPU idle across 3 distinct host-block windows per eval. The existing ms/call meter (`optimizer_manager.cpp:1272-1278`) uses `clock()`, which measures CPU process time and *excludes both GPU time and sync-wait time* — so it systematically under-reads a sync-bound pipeline and cannot arbitrate the claim. The removal order that follows is: (0) instrument with nvtx3 + cudaEvent and measure; (1) async-ify the 3 terminal score copies with a single per-eval event wait (pinned buffers already exist — pure win); (2) batch the DIRECT iteration's independent evals with double-buffered eval state so one eval's tail overlaps the next's head; (3) only if the fragment-fill sync remains dominant, remove it via a device-side clamp + fixed grid (the one kernel-level change); (4) fix the meter to wall-clock/event time. Every cut is gated on the oracle (IoU ≥ 0.85) and, where possible, bit-identical cost values.

* Key Findings

** Sync-point inventory (monoplane eval = 14-15 kernel launches + 5 sync D2H)

Per-eval hot path is `CostFunctionManager::costFunctionDIRECT_DILATION` (src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:67-106): RenderPrimaryCamera → FastImplantDilationMetric → DistanceMapMetric. Kernel/D2H count verified in source:

- Render (`RenderEngine::Render`, src/compute/render_engine.cu:711-840): `cudaMemset` (:716), ResetKernel (:722), WorldToPixelKernel (:725), BoundingBoxForTrianglesKernel (:746), BoundingBoxSizesKernel (:756), `cub::DeviceScan::ExclusiveSum` (:764), PrepareLaunchPacketKernel (:775), StridePrefixKernel (:812), FillTriangleKernel (:823) — 8 launches + cub internals.
- FastImplantDilationMetric (src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:169-295): ResetPixelScoreKernel (:170), EdgeKernel (:218), DilateKernel (:242), DifferenceKernel (:273) — 4 launches.
- DistanceMapMetric (src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu:71-127): 2× Reset (:72,:73) + main kernel (:99) — 3 launches.
- Total ≈ 15 launches (matches the "~15 kernel launches" figure) + 5 synchronous D2H `cudaMemcpy`.
- Biplane adds a full second Render + FastImplantDilationMetric (+11 launches, +3 D2H).
- Confidence: high
- Relevance: this is the count synthesis item 8 was built on; the per-sync *cost* is the part that needs measurement (Cut 0).

The 5 syncs, classified by removability:

| # | file:line | payload | consumer | class |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|-------|
| 1 | render_engine.cu:781-785 | bounding box, 4×int, pinned (`gpu_image.cu:21-22`) | host crop computation for metric launch grids (fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:201-207, distance_map_metric.cu:83-89) | structural mid-eval: host needs bbox to *size* the metric launches; removable only by moving crop to device (kernel change) |
| 2 | render_engine.cu:786-790 | fragment_fill, 1×int, pinned (`render_engine.cu:248-249`) | host overflow check (:795-808) + grid dims of StridePrefix (:812-816) and FillTriangle (:823-827) | structural mid-eval: data-dependent launch; removable via device-side clamp + fixed grid (Cut 3) |
| 3 | fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:289-290 | pixel score, 1×int, pinned (`gpu_metrics.cu:7-11`) | return value of the metric | terminal — async-able now (Cut 1) |
| 4 | distance_map_metric.cu:110-114 | distance_map_score, 1×int, pinned (`gpu_metrics.cu:52-56`) | return value | terminal — async-able now (Cut 1) |
| 5 | distance_map_metric.cu:115-119 | edge_pixels_count, 1×int, pinned (`gpu_metrics.cu:62-65`) | return value | terminal — async-able now (Cut 1) |

Cost nuance: syncs #1 and #2 are back-to-back, so the *fragment* copy (:786-790) waits on the same pipeline drain as the bbox copy and returns almost immediately — the exposed stall is the single drain before them, not two. Similarly #4+#5 share one drain. So the per-eval cost is really ~3 host-block windows (render-head drain, fast-implant drain, distance-map drain), each = GPU idle during host wake + driver launch latency, plus 5× driver round-trip overhead for the sync calls themselves. All targets are already page-locked, so `cudaMemcpyAsync` conversion needs no allocation work.

- Confidence: high
- Relevance: terminal copies (3 of 5) are trivially removable; the 2 render syncs are the structural ones — one of which (fragment_fill) has a clean kernel-level removal, the other (bbox) does not without moving crop math onto the device (which would change launch grids — interaction with 02's metric-math semantics and 04's architecture shape).

** The ms/call meter cannot see GPU time — and under-reads when sync-bound

`optimizer_manager.cpp:1272-1278`:

```cpp
if ((clock() - update_screen_clock_) > 33) {
    emit UpdateDisplay(
        static_cast<double>(clock() - start_clock_) /
            static_cast<double>(opt.GetCostFunctionCalls()),
        ...);
    update_screen_clock_ = clock();
}
```

`clock()` on Linux returns *process CPU time* (user+sys), not wall time. A thread blocked in a synchronous `cudaMemcpy` is sleeping in the driver — it accrues no CPU time. So the meter excludes not only GPU kernel time but also the sync-wait time itself: a sync-bound pipeline reads as *artificially low* ms/call. The meter therefore cannot distinguish "fast" from "GPU idle"; it is directionally misleading for exactly the hypothesis at issue. Any before/after comparison must use a wall-clock meter (std::chrono or cudaEvent), not the existing one.

- Confidence: high (semantics of clock() on Linux; meter code verified)
- Relevance: the user's requirement "a before/after ms/call meter that includes GPU time via events" is not optional polish — the existing meter would fail to show the win, and could even show a *worse* number if a cut moves work from GPU-idle time into CPU time.

** Determinism: int atomicAdd/atomicSub reductions are value-deterministic

All cost-path reductions are integer atomics on single counters:
- DifferenceKernel: `atomicAdd(&result[0], 1)` / `atomicSub(&result[0], 1)` (src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:145,147)
- DistanceMapMetric_Kernel: `atomicAdd(&edge_pixel_count[0], 1)`, `atomicAdd(&distance_map_score[0], distance_map[orig_loc])` (src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu:46-47)
- WhitePixelSum / IOUKernel: `atomicAdd` (src/compute/gpu_metrics.cu:129, src/compute/iou.cu:66-72)

Integer addition is commutative and associative — the final value is independent of execution order. Given identical launch configs and identical inputs, every run yields bit-identical scores. Launch configs depend only on the bounding box (a pure function of pose + model), so the same pose sequence reproduces the same grids and the same results. The known order-nondeterministic path (DRR float atomicAdd) is NOT in the DIRECT_DILATION cost path. Consequences:
1. Bit-identical results after Cuts 1-2 are achievable and verifiable by diffing a recorded pose→score sequence against baseline.
2. Cut 3 must preserve the per-thread work for threads `< fragment_fill` exactly (only add an early-exit clamp for threads `>=`), and must not change the cub scan — then rendered output stays bit-identical.
- Confidence: high
- Relevance: the user's "bit-identical if possible" bar is real; it also gives the oracle a cheap extra gate (compare per-frame optimized pose + cost value to the baseline run, not just IoU).

** Allocation hoisting verified — nothing allocates in the eval path; buffers are pinned

- GPUMetrics ctor allocates all host score buffers via `cudaHostAlloc` and all device score buffers via `cudaMalloc` once (src/compute/gpu_metrics.cu:7-65); destructor frees (same file:68-95).
- RenderEngine::InitializeCUDA allocates all triangle/bounding-box buffers once (src/compute/render_engine.cu:248-323), including CUB scan storage via the size-query idiom (:311-320) — `cub_storage_bytes_` is fixed after init, so the per-eval `cub::DeviceScan::ExclusiveSum` at :764 is a plain launch with no allocation.
- `fragment_fill_` (render_engine.cu:248-249) and `bounding_box_` (src/compute/gpu_image.cu:21-22) are pinned host memory.
- The eval path (`costFunctionDIRECT_DILATION`) performs no cudaMalloc/cudaHostAlloc/free. The per-eval churn is 5 D2H copies, not allocations.
- Confidence: high
- Relevance: Cut 1 (async copies) requires zero allocation work — the pinned targets exist. The "scratch-buffer metrics" ask is already satisfied in the GPU cost path; the per-frame churn the earlier synthesis flagged (GPUImage::UploadImageToGPU reallocating on upload) is outside the eval path.

** nvtx: dependency present, zero instrumentation, and CMake never consumes -DLIBNVTOOLSEXT

- `pixi.toml:17` declares `nvtx = "*"`; the lock resolves it to the *Python* package nvtx-0.2.10 (pixi.lock:257) plus cuda-nvtx-12.4.99 (pixi.lock:63).
- `pixi.toml:76` passes `-DLIBNVTOOLSEXT=$CONDA_PREFIX/lib/libnvToolsExt.so.1` to the configure task, but grep of CMakeLists.txt and src/compute/CMakeLists.txt finds no consumer of that variable — it is dead config. `jtml_compute` links only `CUDA::cublas CUDA::cudart CUDA::curand` (src/compute/CMakeLists.txt:60-65).
- grep for nvtx/nvToolsExt across src/ and include/: zero hits. The scaffolding exists; no markers exist.
- The good news: the C++ nvtx3 API (`<nvtx3/nvtx3.hpp>`) is header-only and ships with the CUDA toolkit; `CMAKE_CUDA_TOOLKIT_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES` is already on jtml_compute's include path (src/compute/CMakeLists.txt:70-72, CMakeLists.txt:64,70), so `#include <nvtx3/nvtx3.hpp>` compiles with *no CMake or link changes*. (The C API `nvtxRangePushA` would need libnvToolsExt linked — avoid it.)
- Nsight availability: `nsight-compute` 2024.1 (ncu) is in the environment (pixi.lock:253); `nsight-systems` (nsys) is NOT (no nsys in pixi.lock) — the profiling plan needs `pixi add nsight-systems` or a system nsys.
- Confidence: high
- Relevance: the "nvtx declared but zero-instrumented" claim verified exactly; the instrumentation plan below is a header include + ~10 range annotations, no build-system surgery.

** The DIRECT loop is sequential, but each iteration's evals are mutually independent — batchable without changing results

`DirectOptimizer::Run` (src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp:27-58) evaluates the unit center once, then loops ConvexHull → TrisectPotentiallyOptimal. In TrisectPotentiallyOptimal (:113-163), for each potentially-optimal hyperbox, two changed-center points are evaluated sequentially:

```cpp
changed_hyperbox_a->value_ = EvaluateCostFunction(changed_hyperbox_a->GetCenter());
data_.AddHyperBox(changed_hyperbox_a);
changed_hyperbox_b->value_ = EvaluateCostFunction(changed_hyperbox_b->GetCenter());
data_.AddHyperBox(changed_hyperbox_b);
```

Both centers derive from the pre-loop snapshot (`potentially_optimal_hyperboxes_`, :116-118); B's pose does not depend on A's score; the loop does not re-enter ConvexHull until all boxes are processed. So per iteration, all 2×N_optimal evals are pairwise independent and can be enqueued back-to-back with a single terminal wait, replaying the per-eval bookkeeping (best-value update + AddHyperBox + improvement callbacks) in the original order afterward — yielding identical stored values, identical optimum, and identical callback sequences. This is the algorithm-level enabler for pipelining; it does not touch GPU code.

- Confidence: high (code path verified; replay-order preserves observable behavior)
- Relevance: this makes the cheapest big win (Cut 2) available without kernel rewrites — matching the user's "per-eval sync removal, not kernel rewrites" lean.

** In-place metric composition constrains streaming: evals must be double-buffered

FastImplantDilationMetric writes *into* the rendered buffer: EdgeKernel writes EDGE_PIXEL into `rendered_image->GetDeviceImagePointer()` (fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:218-240), DilateKernel writes DILATED_PIXEL into it (:242-271), and DistanceMapMetric then reads that same mutated buffer for `EDGE_PIXEL` (distance_map_metric.cu:46-50). Order within an eval is fixed: Render → edge/dilate (in place) → difference (score 1) → distance-map over the edge pixels (score 2). Consequently:
- The two metrics cannot run concurrently on one buffer, and the next eval's Render (`cudaMemset` at render_engine.cu:716) cannot start until the current eval's last metric kernel finishes reading the image.
- Overlapping eval N's tail with eval N+1's head therefore requires a second GPUImage render output (+ duplicate score buffers), i.e. double-buffered eval state. This is the core of the streamed-pipeline design below and the main structural interaction with 04's architecture shape.
- The biplane path has a free overlap: secondary Render uses a different camera's buffers (gpu_model.cu:144-146), so with async terminal copies the primary metrics' D2H overlaps the secondary render kernels on the same stream with no double-buffering.
- Confidence: high
- Relevance: sets the boundary of what streams can buy; single-stream ordering is mostly sufficient once copies are async — the default stream already serializes correctly, so the minimal design needs no multi-stream complexity.

** Miscellaneous hot-path details

- `Render()` opens with `cudaGetLastError()` per eval, self-annotated "MAYBE DELETE TO SAVE TIME?" (render_engine.cu:713) — a per-eval driver round trip, cheap but pointless in a hot loop where the tail of the function already returns `cudaGetLastError()` (:839). Delete it.
- Per-eval pose upload: none. `SetPose` is host-side (render_engine.cu:354-377); WorldToPixelKernel receives pose scalars as kernel arguments (:725-744). No H2D traffic per eval.
- `WriteImage`/`GetcvMatImage` D2H copies (render_engine.cu:852-856, :880-884) are debug/visualization only — off the hot path.
- The fragment-overflow guard is `fragment_fill_[0] > maximum_stride_size * (threads_per_block - 1)` (render_engine.cu:795-808; constants in include/compute/cuda_launch_parameters.h: maximum_stride_size = 10,000,000, threads_per_block = 256) — i.e. the stride-prefix buffer (10M ints, 40 MB) bounds the algorithm at ~2.55G fragments. This check is the reason sync #2 sits mid-eval.
- Confidence: high
- Relevance: cheap wins to fold into Cut 1 (delete the stray cudaGetLastError) and context for the overflow semantics Cut 3 must preserve.

* The streamed-pipeline design

Goal: keep the GPU busy across evals by removing host-block windows, without multi-stream complexity (default-stream ordering already encodes the dependencies).

- **Phase-separated eval API.** Split the cost callback into *enqueue* (launch all kernels + `cudaMemcpyAsync` terminal copies into the existing pinned buffers + `cudaEventRecord`) and *wait* (read scores after the event). For the non-batched path the wait is immediate; for the batched path it is deferred to the end of the iteration.
- **Double-buffered eval state.** Two GPUImage render outputs (or two device images + one swapped GPUImage) plus a second set of dev score buffers (dev_pixel_score_, dev_distance_map_score_, dev_edge_pixels_count_ — either a second GPUMetrics or buffer arrays). Eval A's metric kernels read image A while eval B's Render memset+writes image B.
- **Iteration batching (DirectOptimizer).** New batch surface on the optimizer (e.g. an optional `batch_cost` callback `std::vector<double>(std::vector<Point6D>)` or a deferred-result API): TrisectPotentiallyOptimal collects the iteration's poses, the cost layer enqueues all evals back-to-back (alternating buffers A/B/A/B...), the mid-eval fragment sync of eval k waits while eval k-1's tail runs on the GPU, and one terminal event wait per iteration harvests all scores; bookkeeping replayed in original order (identical values, identical callback sequence).
- **What stays synchronous.** The fragment-fill D2H (render_engine.cu:786-790) remains mid-eval in Cuts 1-2 — but in the batched design its wait overlaps the *previous* eval's already-enqueued kernels, so it stops being an idle bubble. Only Cut 3 removes it entirely.
- **Biplane overlap for free.** Keep the primary metrics' async copies outstanding while enqueuing the secondary Render + FastImplantDilationMetric (different camera buffers, default-stream order is safe); wait once at the end. No double-buffer needed for this one.
- **Streams vs. single stream.** Two explicit streams (copy stream for the D2H + compute stream for kernels, joined by events) are an optional refinement once events exist; the default-stream version captures most of the win with less risk. 04's architecture angle owns the broader backend shape; the seam here is only "eval state is double-buffered and the cost layer can enqueue before it waits."

* nvtx instrumentation plan

Ranges (nvtx3 header-only, `#include <nvtx3/nvtx3.hpp>`, no link/CMake change; compile in always, they are ~ns overhead):

(a) the render drain (bbox+fragment sync + overflow check + launch latency) is the dominant remaining per-eval stall after Cuts 1-2 — e.g., ≥ 50% of per-eval wall (number fixed from Cut 0's table);
(b) the fragment distribution is tightly bounded: max_observed × margin < SAFE_CAP = maximum_stride_size × threads_per_block = 2.55e9 (the capacity ceiling, R2-3), AND a GRID_CAP/256-block launch is affordable (measure the empty-grid launch time for the chosen GRID_CAP — the analytic ceiling would be ~10M blocks, so the practical GRID_CAP comes from the measured distribution, e.g., next power-of-two ≥ max_observed × 2).

Device-side clamp design (R2-3 makes it a host-side change): compute `fill = min(fragment_fill_[0], GRID_CAP)`; launch StridePrefixKernel and FillTriangleKernel from `fill` (ceil(fill/(256×256)) and ceil(fill/256) — the existing launch expressions at render_engine.cu:812-816/:823-826 with the value substituted). Optionally clamp on-device (PrepareLaunchPacketKernel writes min(fragment_fill, GRID_CAP) to a second device int) so the host never needs the true value to launch. NO kernel-source change: threads/blocks beyond the true total exit at the existing in-kernel guards (StridePrefixKernel :592-593; FillTriangleKernel :628-629, which wraps the whole body including the shared-mem load + __syncthreads :636-641), writing nothing. Non-overflow renders are bit-identical by construction (threads < total do exactly today's work).

Overflow semantics preserved (non-negotiable): if fragment_fill_[0] > GRID_CAP, the eval must NOT silently under-render (fragments in (GRID_CAP, total) would never be processed). Two safe behaviors: (i) per-eval fallback to the synchronous read + dynamic grid (the current path — keep the sync as the tail handler), or (ii) abort the frame exactly as today (fragment_overflow_ = true + cudaErrorMemoryAllocation, render_engine.cu:795-808). The fallback keeps bit-identity for all non-fallback evals and preserves error behavior for the tail. The bbox sync (:781-785) is NOT touched by Cut 3 (the crop/grid host math still needs it).

Safe fallback (the decision's default): if (a) or (b) fails — unbounded tail, or GRID_CAP blocks unaffordable — keep the fragment sync and accept it as the one structural cost; in the batched pipeline (Cut 2) its wait already overlaps the previous eval's tail, so the remaining exposure is small. This is a measured no-go, not a punt.

Prediction: Δ = the measured render-drain sum minus the residual fallback cost. Gate: oracle green, non-overflow bit-identity empty, overflow frames still error, event-time reduction ≥ prediction.

### Cut 4 — the event-based ms/call meter (full spec)

Replace BOTH clock() meters: optimizer_manager.cpp:1272-1279 (RunDirectStage iteration callback — the dispatch's :1274-1281) and :1197-1203 (end-of-frame emit). Both currently compute CPU-ticks/call (µs on Linux) and emit it as "ms/call" — CPU-only, GPU-blind, sync-blind, and 1000× unit-wrong (R2-1).

New meter spec:

- wall ms/call = std::chrono::steady_clock elapsed over the stage (RunDirectStage entry → current iteration callback) / opt.GetCostFunctionCalls() — wall INCLUDES GPU time and sync-wait time (the host blocks inside the driver), satisfying "includes GPU time".
- GPU ms/call = the cudaEvent per-eval deltas from Cut 0's instrumentation, accumulated per stage — logged alongside (or the meter owns one minimal event pair per stage if instrumentation is compiled out). wall − GPU = host overhead + sync stalls, reported so the item-8 claim stays visible in the UI's data trail.
- Units: emit TRUE ms/call. The existing UI math then becomes correct without UI changes: "Iterations Per Second: 1000.0 / iteration_speed" (view/mainscreen.cpp:4654-4655) and the ETA (:4598/:4659) both assume ms/call. The fix is at the meter, not the UI.
- Where the UI reads it (verified): UpdateDisplay(double iteration_speed, ...) → OptimizerRunController::onManagerUpdateDisplay (coordinator/optimizer_run_controller.cpp:243) → updateDisplayRelayed → MainScreen::onUpdateDisplay (view/mainscreen.cpp:4582; speed :4654-4655, ETA :4598/:4659, VTK actor text). The QML/experimental path (OptimizerBridge.h) relays no speed today (R2-2) — adding it is a separate small change if the QML UI needs the meter.
- No behavior change to the search. Gate: meter tracks the event-measured per-eval time within noise (wall ≥ event always; the gap is reported, not asserted).

### The measurement protocol every cut must pass

For Cuts 1-3 (Cut 4 is meter-only; Cut 0 is record-only):

(a) headless green — pixi run test (ctest -L headless, --timeout 600; the batch cut adds its Tier-0 replay test to this set);
(b) oracle green — ctest --test-dir .build -L oracle → jtml.oracle: IoU > 0.85 per frame (oracle_test.cpp:333; kIouGate :245, kBudget 3000 :244, TIMEOUT 3600 at test/CMakeLists.txt:1253). Runs only after the synthesis step-1 re-baseline so the gate compares against the trustworthy baseline;
(c) bit-identity diff empty — the pose→score recorder harness: the first 1000 evals of oracle frame 0 recorded as (pose, cost) pairs (recorder at the oracle cost lambda, oracle_test.cpp:288-291); diff vs the baseline recording after each cut. Empty where the cut claims bit-identity (Cuts 1, 2; Cut 3 on non-overflow evals);
(d) measured improvement ≥ prediction — each cut pre-registers its predicted Δ from Cut 0's table (Cut 1: converted-sync stall sum; Cut 2: host-block window sum; Cut 3: render-drain sum); acceptance = mean per-eval event-time reduction over the same 3000-eval sequence ≥ prediction, reproducible over 3 runs.

Revert rule: a cut that measures < prediction (or a regression) is reverted in the same jj change (jj abandon) with the measurement recorded in the run's artifacts; the cut may be retried only with a new prediction derived from the new baseline. Cuts land in order 0 → 1 → 2 → 4 → (3 conditional) — Cut 3 never before Cut 2, Cut 4 before any cut is demonstrated to the user via the UI.

### What Could Not Be Verified (Round 2)

- The actual fragment_fill_ distribution and render-drain times — need the GPU sweep on the RTX 3090 (Cut 0, record item 8). Cut 3's go/no-go is unmeasured until then.
- Whether nvtx3 resolves in the coordinator TUs (include-path question — verify at build; the additive toolkit-include fallback is specified).
- The empty-grid launch cost of a large fixed GRID_CAP (measure at Cut 3 trigger time; the analytic ceiling of ~10M blocks is schedulable but plausibly ms-scale).
- Whether cudaEventSynchronize per eval (Cut 1) still pays a meaningful driver wake-up on this driver/arch — the measurement decides whether Cut 2's restructuring is justified.
- The user-visible magnitude of the R2-1 unit bug (the code path is verified; the numbers on the user's display were not captured).
- GPUMetrics' SetActiveBank semantics vs the three per-stage CFMs sharing one instance (the stage loop is sequential so no interleave by construction, but the invariant is asserted, not yet tested).

### Sources (Round 2)

#+TITLE: Differentiable Polish — gradient-based local refinement after DIRECT, the z-signal, and what is actually transferable to a hand-written CUDA stack
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: differentiable-polish

* Summary

A gradient-polish stage after DIRECT is feasible in this stack, but only if it optimizes a *smooth surrogate* — the production DIRECT_DILATION cost is a piecewise-constant function of pose (binary silhouette + int-atomic reductions), so its gradient is zero almost everywhere and undefined at pixel flips. The surrogate already exists in the codebase: the chamfer distance-map term (DistanceMapMetric), whose gradient is the standard analytic-silhouette-gradient: Σ over rendered edge pixels of ∇D(p)·(projection Jacobian). That Jacobian needs only the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that FillTriangleKernel already computes and throws away. The depth channel is the angle's main myth to puncture: a front-surface z/w buffer is 80% machinery-present (the DRR fill already interpolates perspective-correct z), but a depth channel does *not* make z observable in single-plane fluoro — the 6.31 mm z gap is the magnification limit, and the only real z-fixes are biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior. Verdict: GO for a budget-accounted polish stage (chamfer surrogate, analytic Jacobian, ~2-3 weeks) scored by angle 03's harness as a DIRECT-only vs DIRECT+polish ablation arm; NO-GO for the photometric DRR-gradient and torch-bridge routes.

* Key Findings

** The production cost is piecewise-constant in pose — the gradient of the existing cost is not a usable signal, and this is the load-bearing constraint on everything else
- FastImplantDilationMetric reduces with int atomicAdd over binary comparisons (DILATED_PIXEL/EDGE_PIXEL vs WHITE in the dilated comparison) and DistanceMapMetric sums int distance values over a *discrete* edge-pixel set; both change only when a rendered pixel flips 0↔255 as vertices cross pixel centers. The render itself (RenderEngine::Render) writes a binary silhouette. [Source: repo — src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu, src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu, src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:58-92]
- Consequence: finite-difference on the production cost gives zero or garbage Jacobians for any step not straddling a flip boundary; there is no gradient to "polish" through the production metric. Any polish stage must (a) optimize a smooth surrogate, and (b) verify the result with the production cost — the surrogate is a *search* objective, the production cost stays the *arbiter* (same relationship as angle 03's appearance gate vs cost math).
- Also note the existing metric's int reduction truncates (double→int atomicAdd truncation is already listed as bug 6 in the local recon) — a polish surrogate must use float accumulation.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance to this project: kills option (b) of accountable question 1 (finite-difference on the existing cost) before it starts; forces the surrogate architecture that the harness can actually measure.

** The smooth surrogate already exists: DistanceMapMetric is a chamfer loss, and its gradient is the standard analytic silhouette gradient
- DistanceMapMetric = Σ_{rendered edge pixels} distance_map[p] / (count+0.1) — a mean-chamfer of the rendered silhouette edge to the target (fluoro) edge; the distance transform makes it Lipschitz with an image-space gradient ∇D computable numerically from the distance map itself. [Source: repo — src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu; include/compute/frame.h (SetDistanceMap)]
- The standard differentiable-registration gradient is dL/dθ = Σ_{p ∈ E(θ)} ∇D(p)·(dp/dθ) + a boundary term from pixels crossing the edge set; the boundary term is what analytic AA (Modular Primitives) or soft coverage (SoftRas/DIB-R) smooths, and it is small relative to the ∇D term inside the DIRECT basin (few flips per step at convergence). Published relatives of exactly this gradient: "Analytical Derivatives for Differentiable Renderer: 3D Pose Estimation" (arXiv:1906.07870) and "3D/2D Registration of Angiograms using Silhouette-based Differentiable Rendering" (arXiv:2501.14918). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870; https://arxiv.org/html/2501.14918]
- dp/dθ is analytic for a rigid body: projected p = (fx·X/Z + cx, fy·Y/Z + cy) with (X,Y,Z) affine in the pose θ (R·v + t), so the 2×6 projection Jacobian is a ~50-line kernel. This is the "Modular-Primitives-style analytic silhouette gradient" in its minimal form — no soft rasterizer, no AA pass required for the MVP.
- Confidence: high (the math is standard; the codebase already contains both ingredients)
- Relevance: this is the minimal viable gradient signal (accountable question 1): analytic projection Jacobian + numerical ∇D from the existing distance map, at 1 render per step. The honest baseline to implement *first* (measurement-first) is forward/central differences on this same surrogate (6-12 renders/step, zero new rasterizer code) — it establishes whether gradient polish wins at all before the analytic investment.

** FillTriangleKernel already computes the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that the gradient needs — and discards them
- FillTriangleKernel computes the unnormalized barycentrics (a, b, c, denominator) for the inside test and only writes 255 to the image. Writing (triangleIndex, a, b, c) out for filled pixels is the Modular-Primitives per-pixel output minus the NDC z: exactly the (ID, u, v) tuple the backward pass consumes. The renderer also knows the projected positions and (in the DRR twin) per-vertex camera z, so the un-projected 3D source point of each edge pixel is recoverable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu FillTriangleKernel; Modular Primitives rasterizer outputs (ID, u, v, zc/wc) + 2×2 barycentric Jacobian per https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.03277]
- Cost: one extra device buffer (float4 per filled pixel) + ~10 lines in the fill kernel. The stride/prefix/bounding-box launch scheme is untouched.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance: this is what makes the analytic route cheap — the rasterizer is already 80% of a differentiable rasterizer; only the output staging and the backward scatter-add are missing.

** The depth channel: machinery is 80% present, but a depth channel does NOT fix the z-weak axis in single-plane fluoro — the honest finding this angle exists to deliver
- Where z comes from today: the silhouette path (Render) computes per-vertex camera z (tZ) in WorldToPixelKernel and *discards it*; the DRR path stores it (dev_transf_vertex_zs_) and DRR_FillTriangleKernel interpolates per-pixel perspective-correct z via the rational formula (tvz1·tvz2·tvz3·denominator)/(a·tvz2·tvz3 + b·tvz1·tvz3 + c·tvz1·tvz2) — which is exactly 1/(λ1/z1 + λ2/z2 + λ3/z3), i.e. the perspective-correct interpolated camera z at the pixel. There is no z-testing anywhere (all triangles draw; backfaces are sign-flipped in the DRR accumulation). A front-surface NDC-style depth buffer (this stack's "z/w" ≡ −tZ_cam, positive toward the detector) needs only a min-z test in the fill + a float buffer — and dev_z_line_values_ (width×height float) is already allocated and reusable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu:430-520, src/compute/render_drr_engine.cu DRR_WorldToPixelKernel + DRR_FillTriangleKernel, include/compute/render_engine.cuh dev_z_line_values_/dev_transf_vertex_zs_]
- Why it does not fix z: (a) there is *no target depth* in a single-plane fluoro to compare a rendered depth against — a depth-difference term only exists in synthetic self-supervised ablations (render at known pose → optimize), against a registered bone model / known-geometry prior, or in biplane; (b) the observed z gap is the magnification limit — z-translation is only observable through scale (6.31 mm z gap vs 0.16/0.08 in-plane in baseline.json; angle 03's probe arithmetic: <1% scale change over ±15 mm at ~1.1 m), and no gradient changes what is observable; (c) NVDiffrast — the reference implementation of Modular Primitives — intentionally does *not* backprop through the z/w channel (issue #70: the z/w output's gradients are not propagated; the meaningful gradients are the vertex-position ones). [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json tolerances.observed_max_gap_vs_golden; https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/issues/70 (search-verified content, page fetch failed); https://nvlabs.github.io/nvdiffrast/]
- What the depth machinery IS worth: (i) occlusion-aware visibility gradients — Modular Primitives' premise "a 3D primitive with no effect on the image receives zero gradient" requires knowing which triangle owns each pixel (z-test), which the renderer lacks today; (ii) a synthetic-depth loss in the harness's self-supervised arm (a genuine z test *when a target depth exists*); (iii) the z-line-integral (dev_z_line_values_) is a stronger quantitative z signal than front-depth (it shifts by ≈Δz·path-length under z-translation) but is an X-ray-attenuation proxy — unobservable for a saturated metal implant and only useful in the ML/DRR pathway (DiffDRR-style).
- The real z-fixes: biplane (the codebase already has it — calibration_.convert_Pose_A_to_Pose_B and a biplane branch in DIRECT_DILATION) and the known-geometry prior (implant constrained to a registered bone). This matches the prior-run ML angle's finding 8 ("if the ML pathway is to beat the monoplane z gap, biplane is the evidence-backed direction").
- Confidence: high on the machinery facts (source-verified + NVDiffrast issue); high on the observability argument (analytic); medium on the exact clinical z-benefit of biplane/prior until measured
- Relevance: answer to accountable question 2 — the depth channel is a *gradient-quality and ablation-signal* feature, not a z fix; the harness should test it as such (self-supervised depth arm), and the z-profile probe (angle 03) should first confirm the chamfer surrogate's valley is deeper than the dilated-overlap valley — that is the precondition for any polish z-win.

** Feasibility verdicts per idea (accountable question 1 + 2, with effort/risk — accountable question 3)
- Silhouette-gradient polish on the chamfer surrogate — GO. MVP = forward-difference gradient on the surrogate (6 renders/step, ~1 week) then analytic projection Jacobian + ∇D kernel (1 render/step, +1 week), reusing Render(), the uploaded distance maps, and the injected-cost lambda. Risk medium-low: all machinery exists; the known index-formula bug in distance_map_metric.cu:27 (blockIdx.y+gridDim.x instead of blockIdx.y*gridDim.x) must NOT be copied into new kernels; float accumulation replaces int; match the production backface config (true) and leaf dilation (1) for consistency with verification.
- NDC z/w depth buffer — feasible machinery (+1 week: min-z test + float buffer reuse), but NOT a z fix; only pursue as the enabler for occlusion-aware gradients (visibility gradients) or the synthetic-depth ablation arm. Risk low.
- Analytic AA / occlusion-aware coverage gradient (Modular-Primitives-style, 4×4-style tiles) — research increment (+2-4 weeks) after the MVP shows a win; requires the z-test ownership first. Do not start before measurement.
- Photometric DRR-intensity gradient (DiffDRR-style, hand-written CUDA) — research project (+3-6 weeks, low expected value: the gradient through the atomicAdd z-line-integral is delicate and a saturated metal implant has no usable intensity gradient in the blob interior). NO-GO for now.
- Finite-difference on the *production* cost — NO-GO (piecewise constant, see first finding).
- Torch bridge (thin autograd extension) — NO-GO on convention and merit: torch is *already linked into jtml_compute* (machine_learning_tools.cpp is in the lib, and CostFunctionManager.h even includes <ATen/ops/div_native.h>), so the dependency is not the objection — but for 6-DoF pose of a static STL, autograd buys nothing (the rasterizer backward is a scatter-add; Modular Primitives' core is a CUDA primitive library, torch is only the wrapper) and it violates the documented "no torch in the cost path" design. The ATen include in CostFunctionManager.h is a smell to flag to 04-backend-architecture. [Source: repo — src/compute/CMakeLists.txt:45, include/compute/CostFunctionManager.h, src/compute/machine_learning_tools.cpp]
- CUDA graphs — not for the polish loop: the render engine's stride/prefix/bounding-box scheme launches data-dependent grid shapes per frame (Render() computes launch sizes from fragment_fill_ on the host), which graph capture cannot freeze; that is 05-compute-perf's sync-removal territory for the *existing* path. The polish loop shares Render() unchanged, so it inherits the same 2 D2H syncs/eval — acceptable at ~10^2 polish steps but worth noting 05's win compounds here too.
- Confidence: high on the code facts; medium on effort estimates (single-dev hand-written CUDA, no per-eval timing data yet — 05 will supply it)
- Relevance: the effort/risk table the user asked for; every route reuses the injected-cost boundary and the Render() pipeline, so nothing here forks the architecture.

** The hybrid loop (accountable question 4): a 4th stage after leaf, budget-accounted, seam-unchanged for the MVP
- Loop shape: DIRECT trunk (20k) → 2× branch (5k each) → leaf (5k) → RunPolishStage(current_optimum_location_) → optional re-seed: if polish improves the production cost, run one more leaf-range DIRECT around the polished pose (the DIRECT+local-search re-seed pattern from the literature: Gablonsky's locally-biased DIRECT, the DIRECT+DF-local-search hybrids). [Source: repo — src/coordinator/optimizer_manager.cpp:1031, 1087-1093, 1142-1146 (RunDirectStage call sites); https://repository.lib.ncsu.edu/items/37f7120b-c41e-4267-83d7-5cea4e770b4d; https://optimization-online.org/2014/02/4257/; https://www.research.unipd.it/retrieve/e14fb268-8b47-3de1-e053-1705fe0ac030/OPTE_1039_New_article_2014-OPTE-Liuzzi_etal.pdf]
- Plug-in point: a new OptimizerManager method mirroring RunDirectStage (which is the existing seam — injected-cost lambda at optimizer_manager.cpp:1225+, cumulative SetCallOffset accounting). The MVP needs NO OptimizerRunDriver/OptimizerRunLaunch signature change: the polish reuses the leaf CostFunctionManager (already in the launch payload by value) and adds enable_polish_/polish_budget_/polish_max_steps to OptimizerSettings (mirroring enable_leaf_). Do NOT route through the Stage enum — the always-Trunk guard bug (local-recon bug 4) makes the enum unreliable; call the polish path directly like RunDirectStage is called. [Source: repo — src/coordinator/optimizer_run_driver.cpp:58-100, include/coordinator/optimizer_run_controller.h (OptimizerRunLaunch), include/services/optimizer_settings.h, include/compute/Stage.h, include/compute/CostFunctionManager.h:46]
- Budget semantics: every polish step's surrogate eval and every verification eval must increment cost_function_calls_ so the evals-to-target-IoU comparison (DIRECT-only@B vs DIRECT@(B−B_p)+polish@B_p) is apples-to-apples — the same cumulative-budget discipline angle 03's stage-bookkeeping gate enforces. Progress/stop: reuse the IterationCallback/Stop pattern from RunDirectStage (cooperative stop checked between steps).
- Confidence: high (seam + call sites source-verified)
- Relevance: the OptimizerRunDriver seam hosts the polish stage unchanged, exactly the user's stated requirement; angle 03's multi-stage oracle is the acceptance vehicle.

** The "~12x fewer evals" thesis: an unverified hypothesis with a specific, honest shape — the win is concentrated in the leaf phase, not the total
- Where the thesis would come from: DIRECT's leaf stage spends thousands of evals refining a basin (leaf budget 5000, range ±3 mm) while a gradient method converges in ~10^2 steps on a smooth surrogate — so evals-to-target-IoU can plausibly drop several-fold *in the refinement phase*. But the DIRECT budget is dominated by the global trunk (20k), so a 12x total-budget claim requires the trunk itself to shrink — which is the ML-initializer pathway's job (prior-run ML angle), not the polish's. Realistic expectation to measure: ~1.5-3x on the leaf/refinement phase plus tighter final accuracy and lower frame-to-frame variance. [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json budget_per_stage; analysis of DIRECT vs gradient convergence]
- The harness must therefore report: evals-to-target-IoU (data-profile style, per angle 03's Moré & Wild reference) and per-axis pose gaps for both arms at *equal cumulative budget*, not just final pose. The z-gap band (15.0 mm informational) stays a recorded band, not a gate.
- Confidence: low (thesis is the user's hypothesis; no measurement exists — that is the point of the harness arm)
- Relevance: frames the go/no-go honestly: polish lands only if it wins on the measurement; the 12x figure is a target to test, not a justification.

** Recommended go/no-go for the harness (angle 03's ablation runner as the scoring surface)
- GO: add a "polish" arm to the ablation manifest — same Kneel_1 frames, same production budget shape, two arms: DIRECT-only@B and DIRECT@(B−B_p)+polish@B_p (B_p ≈ leaf-size, e.g. 500-1000 surrogate evals), gated on the IoU ≥ 0.85 appearance gate + per-px L1 band + per-axis gaps recorded into ablation.json (extend the schema angle 03 spec'd with a "polish": {arm, surrogate, steps, evals, final_production_cost} block). Precondition gate: run angle 03's z-profile probe on the chamfer surrogate first — a deeper valley than the dilated-overlap metric is the necessary condition for any z-polish win.
- GO (synthetic, Tier-2-friendly): self-supervised depth arm — render at known poses (Kneel_1 + Study2Grid recipe), optimize from perturbed starts, report per-DOF error split in-plane vs out-of-plane (the Veriserum/DAMN convention from the prior-run ML angle) with and without a synthetic-depth term. This is the only place the depth channel gets a genuine z test.
- NO-GO until the MVP wins: analytic AA, occlusion-aware gradients, NDC depth as a standalone feature, DRR-photometric gradient, torch bridge. Each gets a one-line "deferred pending MVP measurement" in the manifest rather than its own budget.
- Measurement-first guard: the polish stage ships behind a settings flag (enable_polish_) and lands in production only when the ablation arm shows ≥ the IoU gate at equal-or-lower cumulative budget with no per-axis regression — the user's stated rule.
- Confidence: high on the harness mechanics (reuses angle 03's verified instruments); medium on the win (that is what is being measured)
- Relevance: the deliverable the user asked for — a go/no-go the harness can execute without new infrastructure.

** Zotero shortlist (accountable question 5) — pull these 6, in this order of value
1. NVDiffrast code + docs (nvlabs/nvdiffrast, https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast) — the reference CUDA implementation of the Modular-Primitives primitives (AA, vertex-derivative backward scatter-add, the intentional no-gradient-through-z/w policy per issue #70). Highest-value evidence for the exact kernel shapes a hand-written backward needs.

#+TITLE: Differentiable Polish — gradient-based local refinement after DIRECT, the z-signal, and what is actually transferable to a hand-written CUDA stack
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: differentiable-polish

* Summary

A gradient-polish stage after DIRECT is feasible in this stack, but only if it optimizes a *smooth surrogate* — the production DIRECT_DILATION cost is a piecewise-constant function of pose (binary silhouette + int-atomic reductions), so its gradient is zero almost everywhere and undefined at pixel flips. The surrogate already exists in the codebase: the chamfer distance-map term (DistanceMapMetric), whose gradient is the standard analytic-silhouette-gradient: Σ over rendered edge pixels of ∇D(p)·(projection Jacobian). That Jacobian needs only the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that FillTriangleKernel already computes and throws away. The depth channel is the angle's main myth to puncture: a front-surface z/w buffer is 80% machinery-present (the DRR fill already interpolates perspective-correct z), but a depth channel does *not* make z observable in single-plane fluoro — the 6.31 mm z gap is the magnification limit, and the only real z-fixes are biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior. Verdict: GO for a budget-accounted polish stage (chamfer surrogate, analytic Jacobian, ~2-3 weeks) scored by angle 03's harness as a DIRECT-only vs DIRECT+polish ablation arm; NO-GO for the photometric DRR-gradient and torch-bridge routes.

* Key Findings

** The production cost is piecewise-constant in pose — the gradient of the existing cost is not a usable signal, and this is the load-bearing constraint on everything else
- FastImplantDilationMetric reduces with int atomicAdd over binary comparisons (DILATED_PIXEL/EDGE_PIXEL vs WHITE in the dilated comparison) and DistanceMapMetric sums int distance values over a *discrete* edge-pixel set; both change only when a rendered pixel flips 0↔255 as vertices cross pixel centers. The render itself (RenderEngine::Render) writes a binary silhouette. [Source: repo — src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu, src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu, src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:58-92]
- Consequence: finite-difference on the production cost gives zero or garbage Jacobians for any step not straddling a flip boundary; there is no gradient to "polish" through the production metric. Any polish stage must (a) optimize a smooth surrogate, and (b) verify the result with the production cost — the surrogate is a *search* objective, the production cost stays the *arbiter* (same relationship as angle 03's appearance gate vs cost math).
- Also note the existing metric's int reduction truncates (double→int atomicAdd truncation is already listed as bug 6 in the local recon) — a polish surrogate must use float accumulation.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance to this project: kills option (b) of accountable question 1 (finite-difference on the existing cost) before it starts; forces the surrogate architecture that the harness can actually measure.

** The smooth surrogate already exists: DistanceMapMetric is a chamfer loss, and its gradient is the standard analytic silhouette gradient
- DistanceMapMetric = Σ_{rendered edge pixels} distance_map[p] / (count+0.1) — a mean-chamfer of the rendered silhouette edge to the target (fluoro) edge; the distance transform makes it Lipschitz with an image-space gradient ∇D computable numerically from the distance map itself. [Source: repo — src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu; include/compute/frame.h (SetDistanceMap)]
- The standard differentiable-registration gradient is dL/dθ = Σ_{p ∈ E(θ)} ∇D(p)·(dp/dθ) + a boundary term from pixels crossing the edge set; the boundary term is what analytic AA (Modular Primitives) or soft coverage (SoftRas/DIB-R) smooths, and it is small relative to the ∇D term inside the DIRECT basin (few flips per step at convergence). Published relatives of exactly this gradient: "Analytical Derivatives for Differentiable Renderer: 3D Pose Estimation" (arXiv:1906.07870) and "3D/2D Registration of Angiograms using Silhouette-based Differentiable Rendering" (arXiv:2501.14918). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870; https://arxiv.org/html/2501.14918]
- dp/dθ is analytic for a rigid body: projected p = (fx·X/Z + cx, fy·Y/Z + cy) with (X,Y,Z) affine in the pose θ (R·v + t), so the 2×6 projection Jacobian is a ~50-line kernel. This is the "Modular-Primitives-style analytic silhouette gradient" in its minimal form — no soft rasterizer, no AA pass required for the MVP.
- Confidence: high (the math is standard; the codebase already contains both ingredients)
- Relevance: this is the minimal viable gradient signal (accountable question 1): analytic projection Jacobian + numerical ∇D from the existing distance map, at 1 render per step. The honest baseline to implement *first* (measurement-first) is forward/central differences on this same surrogate (6-12 renders/step, zero new rasterizer code) — it establishes whether gradient polish wins at all before the analytic investment.

** FillTriangleKernel already computes the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that the gradient needs — and discards them
- FillTriangleKernel computes the unnormalized barycentrics (a, b, c, denominator) for the inside test and only writes 255 to the image. Writing (triangleIndex, a, b, c) out for filled pixels is the Modular-Primitives per-pixel output minus the NDC z: exactly the (ID, u, v) tuple the backward pass consumes. The renderer also knows the projected positions and (in the DRR twin) per-vertex camera z, so the un-projected 3D source point of each edge pixel is recoverable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu FillTriangleKernel; Modular Primitives rasterizer outputs (ID, u, v, zc/wc) + 2×2 barycentric Jacobian per https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.03277]
- Cost: one extra device buffer (float4 per filled pixel) + ~10 lines in the fill kernel. The stride/prefix/bounding-box launch scheme is untouched.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance: this is what makes the analytic route cheap — the rasterizer is already 80% of a differentiable rasterizer; only the output staging and the backward scatter-add are missing.

** The depth channel: machinery is 80% present, but a depth channel does NOT fix the z-weak axis in single-plane fluoro — the honest finding this angle exists to deliver
- Where z comes from today: the silhouette path (Render) computes per-vertex camera z (tZ) in WorldToPixelKernel and *discards it*; the DRR path stores it (dev_transf_vertex_zs_) and DRR_FillTriangleKernel interpolates per-pixel perspective-correct z via the rational formula (tvz1·tvz2·tvz3·denominator)/(a·tvz2·tvz3 + b·tvz1·tvz3 + c·tvz1·tvz2) — which is exactly 1/(λ1/z1 + λ2/z2 + λ3/z3), i.e. the perspective-correct interpolated camera z at the pixel. There is no z-testing anywhere (all triangles draw; backfaces are sign-flipped in the DRR accumulation). A front-surface NDC-style depth buffer (this stack's "z/w" ≡ −tZ_cam, positive toward the detector) needs only a min-z test in the fill + a float buffer — and dev_z_line_values_ (width×height float) is already allocated and reusable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu:430-520, src/compute/render_drr_engine.cu DRR_WorldToPixelKernel + DRR_FillTriangleKernel, include/compute/render_engine.cuh dev_z_line_values_/dev_transf_vertex_zs_]
- Why it does not fix z: (a) there is *no target depth* in a single-plane fluoro to compare a rendered depth against — a depth-difference term only exists in synthetic self-supervised ablations (render at known pose → optimize), against a registered bone model / known-geometry prior, or in biplane; (b) the observed z gap is the magnification limit — z-translation is only observable through scale (6.31 mm z gap vs 0.16/0.08 in-plane in baseline.json; angle 03's probe arithmetic: <1% scale change over ±15 mm at ~1.1 m), and no gradient changes what is observable; (c) NVDiffrast — the reference implementation of Modular Primitives — intentionally does *not* backprop through the z/w channel (issue #70: the z/w output's gradients are not propagated; the meaningful gradients are the vertex-position ones). [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json tolerances.observed_max_gap_vs_golden; https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/issues/70 (search-verified content, page fetch failed); https://nvlabs.github.io/nvdiffrast/]
- What the depth machinery IS worth: (i) occlusion-aware visibility gradients — Modular Primitives' premise "a 3D primitive with no effect on the image receives zero gradient" requires knowing which triangle owns each pixel (z-test), which the renderer lacks today; (ii) a synthetic-depth loss in the harness's self-supervised arm (a genuine z test *when a target depth exists*); (iii) the z-line-integral (dev_z_line_values_) is a stronger quantitative z signal than front-depth (it shifts by ≈Δz·path-length under z-translation) but is an X-ray-attenuation proxy — unobservable for a saturated metal implant and only useful in the ML/DRR pathway (DiffDRR-style).
- The real z-fixes: biplane (the codebase already has it — calibration_.convert_Pose_A_to_Pose_B and a biplane branch in DIRECT_DILATION) and the known-geometry prior (implant constrained to a registered bone). This matches the prior-run ML angle's finding 8 ("if the ML pathway is to beat the monoplane z gap, biplane is the evidence-backed direction").
- Confidence: high on the machinery facts (source-verified + NVDiffrast issue); high on the observability argument (analytic); medium on the exact clinical z-benefit of biplane/prior until measured
- Relevance: answer to accountable question 2 — the depth channel is a *gradient-quality and ablation-signal* feature, not a z fix; the harness should test it as such (self-supervised depth arm), and the z-profile probe (angle 03) should first confirm the chamfer surrogate's valley is deeper than the dilated-overlap valley — that is the precondition for any polish z-win.

** Feasibility verdicts per idea (accountable question 1 + 2, with effort/risk — accountable question 3)
- Silhouette-gradient polish on the chamfer surrogate — GO. MVP = forward-difference gradient on the surrogate (6 renders/step, ~1 week) then analytic projection Jacobian + ∇D kernel (1 render/step, +1 week), reusing Render(), the uploaded distance maps, and the injected-cost lambda. Risk medium-low: all machinery exists; the known index-formula bug in distance_map_metric.cu:27 (blockIdx.y+gridDim.x instead of blockIdx.y*gridDim.x) must NOT be copied into new kernels; float accumulation replaces int; match the production backface config (true) and leaf dilation (1) for consistency with verification.
- NDC z/w depth buffer — feasible machinery (+1 week: min-z test + float buffer reuse), but NOT a z fix; only pursue as the enabler for occlusion-aware gradients (visibility gradients) or the synthetic-depth ablation arm. Risk low.
- Analytic AA / occlusion-aware coverage gradient (Modular-Primitives-style, 4×4-style tiles) — research increment (+2-4 weeks) after the MVP shows a win; requires the z-test ownership first. Do not start before measurement.
- Photometric DRR-intensity gradient (DiffDRR-style, hand-written CUDA) — research project (+3-6 weeks, low expected value: the gradient through the atomicAdd z-line-integral is delicate and a saturated metal implant has no usable intensity gradient in the blob interior). NO-GO for now.
- Finite-difference on the *production* cost — NO-GO (piecewise constant, see first finding).
- Torch bridge (thin autograd extension) — NO-GO on convention and merit: torch is *already linked into jtml_compute* (machine_learning_tools.cpp is in the lib, and CostFunctionManager.h even includes <ATen/ops/div_native.h>), so the dependency is not the objection — but for 6-DoF pose of a static STL, autograd buys nothing (the rasterizer backward is a scatter-add; Modular Primitives' core is a CUDA primitive library, torch is only the wrapper) and it violates the documented "no torch in the cost path" design. The ATen include in CostFunctionManager.h is a smell to flag to 04-backend-architecture. [Source: repo — src/compute/CMakeLists.txt:45, include/compute/CostFunctionManager.h, src/compute/machine_learning_tools.cpp]
- CUDA graphs — not for the polish loop: the render engine's stride/prefix/bounding-box scheme launches data-dependent grid shapes per frame (Render() computes launch sizes from fragment_fill_ on the host), which graph capture cannot freeze; that is 05-compute-perf's sync-removal territory for the *existing* path. The polish loop shares Render() unchanged, so it inherits the same 2 D2H syncs/eval — acceptable at ~10^2 polish steps but worth noting 05's win compounds here too.
- Confidence: high on the code facts; medium on effort estimates (single-dev hand-written CUDA, no per-eval timing data yet — 05 will supply it)
- Relevance: the effort/risk table the user asked for; every route reuses the injected-cost boundary and the Render() pipeline, so nothing here forks the architecture.

** The hybrid loop (accountable question 4): a 4th stage after leaf, budget-accounted, seam-unchanged for the MVP
- Loop shape: DIRECT trunk (20k) → 2× branch (5k each) → leaf (5k) → RunPolishStage(current_optimum_location_) → optional re-seed: if polish improves the production cost, run one more leaf-range DIRECT around the polished pose (the DIRECT+local-search re-seed pattern from the literature: Gablonsky's locally-biased DIRECT, the DIRECT+DF-local-search hybrids). [Source: repo — src/coordinator/optimizer_manager.cpp:1031, 1087-1093, 1142-1146 (RunDirectStage call sites); https://repository.lib.ncsu.edu/items/37f7120b-c41e-4267-83d7-5cea4e770b4d; https://optimization-online.org/2014/02/4257/; https://www.research.unipd.it/retrieve/e14fb268-8b47-3de1-e053-1705fe0ac030/OPTE_1039_New_article_2014-OPTE-Liuzzi_etal.pdf]
- Plug-in point: a new OptimizerManager method mirroring RunDirectStage (which is the existing seam — injected-cost lambda at optimizer_manager.cpp:1225+, cumulative SetCallOffset accounting). The MVP needs NO OptimizerRunDriver/OptimizerRunLaunch signature change: the polish reuses the leaf CostFunctionManager (already in the launch payload by value) and adds enable_polish_/polish_budget_/polish_max_steps to OptimizerSettings (mirroring enable_leaf_). Do NOT route through the Stage enum — the always-Trunk guard bug (local-recon bug 4) makes the enum unreliable; call the polish path directly like RunDirectStage is called. [Source: repo — src/coordinator/optimizer_run_driver.cpp:58-100, include/coordinator/optimizer_run_controller.h (OptimizerRunLaunch), include/services/optimizer_settings.h, include/compute/Stage.h, include/compute/CostFunctionManager.h:46]
- Budget semantics: every polish step's surrogate eval and every verification eval must increment cost_function_calls_ so the evals-to-target-IoU comparison (DIRECT-only@B vs DIRECT@(B−B_p)+polish@B_p) is apples-to-apples — the same cumulative-budget discipline angle 03's stage-bookkeeping gate enforces. Progress/stop: reuse the IterationCallback/Stop pattern from RunDirectStage (cooperative stop checked between steps).

This is a pixel-grid kernel (not the fragment stream) deliberately: it processes each pixel once, which dedupes the overlapping-triangle case that a fragment-stream iteration would double-count (R2-3's last-writer attribute resolves ownership). [Source: repo — src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu (crop formula), src/compute/render_engine.cu (fragment stream semantics)]
- Float accumulation + the determinism rule (the part that is easy to get wrong): the gradient MUST accumulate in float (never the production path's int truncation — the distance-map index bug and the int-atomic truncation are explicitly NOT to be copied), AND the accumulation must be bit-deterministic, because the ablation runner's rerun_identical determinism twin (ablation.json determinism block) would trip on a float-atomic gradient — Contradiction 3's int-determinism doctrine extends to the polish by construction. Design: per-block shared-memory reduction to 6 floats → dev_chamfer_gradient_partials_[6·nBlocks] (≈24 KB at nBlocks ≈ 1000) → a second 1-block kernel reduces the partials in fixed block order → the 6-float gradient. Two kernels, ~30 lines; float atomicAdd into the partial array is acceptable ONLY if the run records the gradient hash as informational — spec the ordered reduction as the default. Reset via cudaMemset before each call (6·(1+nBlocks)·4 B ≈ 24 KB — cheap, and the eval path's no-cudaMalloc rule is preserved: the partial array is allocated once in the polish stage's initialization). [Source: repo — test/golden/ablation.json schema (angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org R2-4 determinism block); synthesis Contradiction 3]

- The round-1 two-arm design had a confound this round's redesign removes: DIRECT-only@B vs DIRECT@(B−B_p)+polish@B_p cannot separate "polish added quality" from "the 1000 evals were spent better by polish than DIRECT would have spent them" — the budget gift itself is the alternative explanation. The pre-registered design is therefore three arms, all from the same start seed, all on the same frame:
  - **A: DIRECT-only@35k** (production shape 20/25/30/35k) — the reference.
  - **B: DIRECT-only@34k** (leaf 5000→4000; cumulative 20/25/30/34k) — the budget-gift control: it is what DIRECT does with the budget BEFORE the polish gets it.
  - **C: DIRECT@34k + polish@B_p = 1000** (DIRECT as in B, then RunPolishStage at the leaf optimum; polish evals push the counter to 35k).
  C wins only if C beats B (polish used its 1000 evals better than DIRECT would have — the marginal-value test) AND C ≥ A (no net loss at equal total budget — the equal-budget test). If C > B but C < A, polish added nothing net: the 1000 evals were better spent by DIRECT. This is the honest arbitrage of the "12x" thesis: at FIXED total budget the thesis reduces to a final-quality comparison; the "fewer evals" reading only materializes when the DIRECT budget itself shrinks (the ML-initializer pathway), which the arm records but does not claim. #+TITLE: Panoptes Research: Optimizer Deep-Dive — Architecture + Algorithm Upgrades
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+RESEARCH_ANGLES: 6
#+ROUND: 2 (wave 1) — angles 01–04 deepened with '## Round 2' sections; 05/06 deferred to wave 2
#+STATUS: complete

* Executive Summary

The single highest-leverage finding of this run: **the current 0.9936 IoU baseline is measured against a deterministically-corrupted cost term.** Angle 02 verified at the dispatch's line numbers that the distance-map index formula (distance_map_metric.cu:27, `blockIdx.y + gridDim.x` instead of `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`) mis-maps every block row, so the distance-map term of every DIRECT_DILATION oracle evaluation accumulates at the wrong pixels. That is the one live bug of the seven verified — the other six poison latent paths only. Fixing it and re-baselining (one single re-baseline after all behavior-neutral fixes land) is the prerequisite for every other decision in this run: variant switches, perf cuts, and gradient polish are all judged against a baseline that is not trustworthy until this lands. The gate (IoU ≥ 0.85) is far below the measured 0.9936, so the appearance arbiter stays, but measured IoU / per-px L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap are informational and expected to move.

Round 2 sharpened the critical path in an important way: the corrupted index has **exactly one reader** (DistanceMapMetric_Kernel, invoked only from DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80), and every post-optimize measurement metric (IoU, per-px L1, chamfer) uses the correct formula — so the 0.9936/0.0207 numbers themselves are not corrupted, only the cost that drove the search. The corruption is a systematic exclusion: the top ~64 crop rows of the rendered band are never sampled and the middle band is multiplicity-over-weighted, so the distance-map term is *flatter in z* than the honest chamfer complement. The structural prediction is that the re-baselined DIRECT optimum moves toward the golden z and the frame-1 6.31 mm z gap shrinks materially (direction: medium-high confidence; magnitude: not predictable without the GPU re-run).

The recommended course of action, in dependency order, is unchanged in shape and updated in content: (1) pin-first fixes per angle 02 (Tier-0 pins, behavior-neutral fixes, the distance-map index fix + one oracle re-baseline — plus the new CUDA-free finite-check at DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction, needed regardless of GLh); (2) the measurement apparatus per angle 03 — the z-profile probe on the RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda (now an executable 31-render spec) and the production-shaped multi-stage oracle through the plan-006 OptimizerRunDriver seam, which **no longer needs the "small seam addition"**: Round 2 proved Directive::SymTrap already exists in the typed enum, so the tibia-ambiguity pass is three pins, not a code change; (3) the ablation runner + ablation.json (schema now complete, plus the perturbation suite that calibrates the IoU gate's checked coverage); (4) the evidence-backed algorithm upgrade from angle 01 — **1-DTC-GL-gb** — now with a concrete analytic battery (22 n=5 problems + Hartman6, GKLS classes, pe≤1e-2), a quantified split tie-break divergence (a faithful GL landing requires switching the repo's largest-denormalized-side rule to the study's least-split rule), and a gb-semantics caveat (the DIRECTGO reference code toggles the phases inverted relative to the paper's prose — implement the canonical semantics plus an ablation arm replicating the code as shipped); (5) compute-perf cuts 0–4 per angle 05, gated on oracle green and bit-identical cost values; (6) the differentiable-polish stage per angle 06, GO-gated on the z-profile probe and an ablation arm. Architecture work (angle 04) flows through as additive cuts A–F.

Two tensions the user should carry explicitly. First, **the variant switch cannot fix the z-axis**: Round 2 resolved this from a scoping tension into an explicit mechanism analysis — the variant choice (search scheme) and the z-sensitivity ranking (cost observability) are orthogonal in mechanism, with only two documented second-order interactions (the NaN/Inf trigger and refinement-control savings on z-flat costs); the harness must report evals and z-error separately, and a variant-switch win must never be read as a z fix. The real z remedies remain biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior, and every z remedy is gated on angle 03's probe. Second, **perf cuts do not sacrifice determinism**: every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd (order-independent, value-deterministic), so async copies and iteration batching can preserve bit-identical results; angle 04's Round-2 seam contract pins the double-buffered eval state (compute owns the buffer state, the manager owns the object graph, the domain sees only std::function).

Round 2 also closed the run's longest-standing open question: **the DIRECT-GLh NaN trigger is now resolved per-variant.** DIRECT_DILATION is structurally incapable of emitting NaN/Inf (all-int composition, +0.1-guarded division, max accumulation 2.55e8 ≪ 2³¹) — the GLh trigger lives in DIRECT_MAHFOUZ (0/0 via the pointer-guard bug, production-reachable), DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT (UB min_dist), and sym_trap (asin domain). The finite-check belongs at the one shared chokepoint, DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction (direct_optimizer.cpp:205), and the round-1 claim that "NaN poisons hull slope comparisons" is corrected: NaN boxes accumulate as dead weight at the column front (lost evals, unbounded growth), with the column minimum poisoned only after all finite boxes are trisected away — a delayed, conditional effect, still worth closing. The "12x fewer evals" polish thesis remains a target to test, not a justification: angle 06's analysis puts the realistic win at ~1.5–3× in the leaf/refinement phase, with the chamfer distance-map surrogate as the one smooth gradient signal. Everything else from the papers — 1-DTDV boundary sampling, analytic-AA occlusion gradients, DRR-photometric gradients, torch bridges — stays conditional, deferred, or NO-GO, and each lands only through the harness.

#+TITLE: Panoptes Research: Optimizer Deep-Dive — Architecture + Algorithm Upgrades
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+RESEARCH_ANGLES: 6
#+ROUND: 2 (wave 1) — angles 01–04 deepened with '## Round 2' sections; 05/06 deferred to wave 2
#+STATUS: complete

* Executive Summary

The single highest-leverage finding of this run: **the current 0.9936 IoU baseline is measured against a deterministically-corrupted cost term.** Angle 02 verified at the dispatch's line numbers that the distance-map index formula (distance_map_metric.cu:27, `blockIdx.y + gridDim.x` instead of `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`) mis-maps every block row, so the distance-map term of every DIRECT_DILATION oracle evaluation accumulates at the wrong pixels. That is the one live bug of the seven verified — the other six poison latent paths only. Fixing it and re-baselining (one single re-baseline after all behavior-neutral fixes land) is the prerequisite for every other decision in this run: variant switches, perf cuts, and gradient polish are all judged against a baseline that is not trustworthy until this lands. The gate (IoU ≥ 0.85) is far below the measured 0.9936, so the appearance arbiter stays, but measured IoU / per-px L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap are informational and expected to move.

Round 2 sharpened the critical path in an important way: the corrupted index has **exactly one reader** (DistanceMapMetric_Kernel, invoked only from DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80), and every post-optimize measurement metric (IoU, per-px L1, chamfer) uses the correct formula — so the 0.9936/0.0207 numbers themselves are not corrupted, only the cost that drove the search. The corruption is a systematic exclusion: the top ~64 crop rows of the rendered band are never sampled and the middle band is multiplicity-over-weighted, so the distance-map term is *flatter in z* than the honest chamfer complement. The structural prediction is that the re-baselined DIRECT optimum moves toward the golden z and the frame-1 6.31 mm z gap shrinks materially (direction: medium-high confidence; magnitude: not predictable without the GPU re-run).

The recommended course of action, in dependency order, is unchanged in shape and updated in content: (1) pin-first fixes per angle 02 (Tier-0 pins, behavior-neutral fixes, the distance-map index fix + one oracle re-baseline — plus the new CUDA-free finite-check at DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction, needed regardless of GLh); (2) the measurement apparatus per angle 03 — the z-profile probe on the RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda (now an executable 31-render spec) and the production-shaped multi-stage oracle through the plan-006 OptimizerRunDriver seam, which **no longer needs the "small seam addition"**: Round 2 proved Directive::SymTrap already exists in the typed enum, so the tibia-ambiguity pass is three pins, not a code change; (3) the ablation runner + ablation.json (schema now complete, plus the perturbation suite that calibrates the IoU gate's checked coverage); (4) the evidence-backed algorithm upgrade from angle 01 — **1-DTC-GL-gb** — now with a concrete analytic battery (22 n=5 problems + Hartman6, GKLS classes, pe≤1e-2), a quantified split tie-break divergence (a faithful GL landing requires switching the repo's largest-denormalized-side rule to the study's least-split rule), and a gb-semantics caveat (the DIRECTGO reference code toggles the phases inverted relative to the paper's prose — implement the canonical semantics plus an ablation arm replicating the code as shipped); (5) compute-perf cuts 0–4 per angle 05, gated on oracle green and bit-identical cost values; (6) the differentiable-polish stage per angle 06, GO-gated on the z-profile probe and an ablation arm. Architecture work (angle 04) flows through as additive cuts A–F.

Two tensions the user should carry explicitly. First, **the variant switch cannot fix the z-axis**: Round 2 resolved this from a scoping tension into an explicit mechanism analysis — the variant choice (search scheme) and the z-sensitivity ranking (cost observability) are orthogonal in mechanism, with only two documented second-order interactions (the NaN/Inf trigger and refinement-control savings on z-flat costs); the harness must report evals and z-error separately, and a variant-switch win must never be read as a z fix. The real z remedies remain biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior, and every z remedy is gated on angle 03's probe. Second, **perf cuts do not sacrifice determinism**: every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd (order-independent, value-deterministic), so async copies and iteration batching can preserve bit-identical results; angle 04's Round-2 seam contract pins the double-buffered eval state (compute owns the buffer state, the manager owns the object graph, the domain sees only std::function).

Round 2 also closed the run's longest-standing open question: **the DIRECT-GLh NaN trigger is now resolved per-variant.** DIRECT_DILATION is structurally incapable of emitting NaN/Inf (all-int composition, +0.1-guarded division, max accumulation 2.55e8 ≪ 2³¹) — the GLh trigger lives in DIRECT_MAHFOUZ (0/0 via the pointer-guard bug, production-reachable), DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT (UB min_dist), and sym_trap (asin domain). The finite-check belongs at the one shared chokepoint, DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction (direct_optimizer.cpp:205), and the round-1 claim that "NaN poisons hull slope comparisons" is corrected: NaN boxes accumulate as dead weight at the column front (lost evals, unbounded growth), with the column minimum poisoned only after all finite boxes are trisected away — a delayed, conditional effect, still worth closing. The "12x fewer evals" polish thesis remains a target to test, not a justification: angle 06's analysis puts the realistic win at ~1.5–3× in the leaf/refinement phase, with the chamfer distance-map surrogate as the one smooth gradient signal. Everything else from the papers — 1-DTDV boundary sampling, analytic-AA occlusion gradients, DRR-photometric gradients, torch bridges — stays conditional, deferred, or NO-GO, and each lands only through the harness.

Design: `if (!std::isfinite(result)) { non_finite_count_++; /* GLh: result = f_min + d(x,x_min) when enabled; else treat as infeasible (do not store, never wins the optimum) */ }` plus GetNonFiniteCount() and an iteration-callback event. The GPU side needs NO checks — all GPU outputs are provably finite ints. Probes: Tier-0 headless (fake cost lambda returning NaN/±Inf/sNaN; asserts no crash, counter increments, optimum never reflects a non-finite eval, GLh surrogate behavior, surviving columns finite) and Tier-2 GPU (sanity sweep golden ± range ~61 evals; adversarial poses ±200 mm off-axis, behind camera, 90°/180° rotations; assert finite AND cudaGetLastError() == cudaSuccess after each eval — the sticky-error trap at render_engine.cu:713; DIRECT_MAHFOUZ at an empty-silhouette pose EXPECT NaN today, green after the guard fix). [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2]
